observations.title: sdd/v2-01-identity/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: V2-01 Identity (F1, 🔥 HOT)

> ROADMAP.md §3 F1 (change V2-01), traps #3 (multitenant isolation) and #11 (open-registration abuse). Judgment-day (2 blind judges) required before archive. Canonical file: openspec/changes/v2-01-identity/proposal.md (hybrid).

## Intent
v1 shipped an IDOR because query scoping was optional (trap #3). V2-01 delivers the multitenant identity layer — org membership, invitations, module access, a single `withOrg()` scoping helper — plus abuse-mitigation mechanisms (trap #11), and fixes the confirmed invited-user orphan-org hazard in `ensure-owner-organization` (explore §2).

## Scope
IN: member_module_access table (module, nullable store) + withOrg() in shared/db callable ONLY from module public APIs, isolation.test.ts written first (red) as enforcing gate; invitation lifecycle via better-auth org plugin + Resend (RESEND_API_KEY optional, dev log stub); orphan-org fix (pending unexpired invitation check by email inside ensure-owner-organization before auto-creation; activeOrganizationId stays null until invite resolution; post-registration "accept your invitation" UX); abuse MECHANISM only (email-verification enforcement infra + Postgres rate_limit_bucket fixed-window limiter on register + costly endpoints; no new blocking of user actions in V2-01); minimal shadcn UI (org settings, members list, invite flow, two-level role editor); seed second org + invited member fixtures.
OUT: trial-credit gating policy, billing, credit ledger, admin alerts (V2-02+); org deletion (deferred — no flow needs it pre-billing, cascade semantics would be designed twice once credit ledger lands); domain tables of other modules.

## Capabilities
NEW: `org-membership` (orgs, roles owner|admin|member, invitation lifecycle incl. invited-user registration path); `module-access` (member_module_access + withOrg() scoping + cross-org isolation guarantees); `abuse-mitigation-mechanism` (verification-enforcement infra + Postgres fixed-window rate limiting; mechanism only, policy in V2-02).
MODIFIED: `auth-foundation` — (1) registration auto-org creation conditional (skipped when pending unexpired invitation matches email); (2) "session carries non-null activeOrganizationId" relaxed — null allowed while invitation unresolved.

## Approach
Use better-auth org plugin free surface (org/member CRUD, invite endpoints, hasPermission, sendInvitationEmail, expiry). Build only what it lacks: member_module_access, withOrg() (fork A shaped for B, explore §5), rate_limit_bucket UPSERT limiter, enforcement toggle, fixtures, UI. Strict TDD; isolation.test.ts first.

## Affected Areas
- src/shared/auth/ensure-owner-organization.ts — Modified (pending-invitation check; highest-risk change)
- src/shared/auth/auth.ts — Modified (sendInvitationEmail, organizationHooks, verification toggle)
- src/modules/identity/* — Modified (export withOrg, member/invitation APIs, UI)
- src/shared/db/schema/* — New (member_module_access, rate_limit_bucket + migrations)
- src/shared/env — Modified (optional RESEND_API_KEY)
- seed steps — Modified (second org + invited member)

## Risks
- ensure-owner-organization edit regresses V2-00's most safety-critical code (Med) → its existing unit+integration suite is the regression net; extend, never weaken.
- Forgotten withOrg() call = silent IDOR (Med) → callable only from module index.ts + isolation.test.ts red-first.
- Null activeOrganizationId breaks session assumptions (Med) → explicit UX branch; session enrichment resolves after accept; rejected/expired invite falls back to auto-creation.
- Rate-limiter contention (Low) → single-row UPSERT per (key, window).

## Rollback Plan
Single change branch → revert PR. Migrations additive (member_module_access, rate_limit_bucket droppable). ensure-owner-organization fix is pure code revert. No data backfill (no production users — ROADMAP decision #1).

## Dependencies
Depends on archived V2-00 (auth-foundation, project-scaffold). Blocks V2-02 billing (needs verified-email + rate-limit mechanisms and org identity). ROADMAP §2 graph.

## Success Criteria
- isolation.test.ts green — THE gate (org A never reads/writes org B via any exported identity API).
- Invited-user E2E: register with pending invite → no orphan org → accept → activeOrganizationId set.
- docker compose up local + E2E suite green (ROADMAP #10).
- V2-00 auth-foundation test suite still green.
- verify PASS, then judgment-day (2 blind judges) PASS before archive.

observations.title: sdd/v2-01-identity/spec
observations.content:
# Spec Delta: v2-01-identity

> Source: proposal.md. Capabilities: NEW org-membership, module-access,
> abuse-mitigation-mechanism; MODIFIED auth-foundation.
> Multitenant isolation scenario included per config.yaml `rules.specs`.
> Full file: openspec/changes/v2-01-identity/spec.md

## Capability: `org-membership` (NEW)

### Requirement: Organization membership and roles
The system MUST support organization membership records with role
`owner | admin | member`, enforced via better-auth's organization plugin
member CRUD and `hasPermission`.

#### Scenario: Owner manages members
- GIVEN an authenticated owner of org A
- WHEN they list, update the role of, or remove a member of org A
- THEN the operation succeeds and is scoped to org A only

#### Scenario: Member cannot manage other members
- GIVEN an authenticated member (non-admin) of org A
- WHEN they attempt to remove or change the role of another member
- THEN the request is denied with a permission error

### Requirement: Invitation lifecycle
The system MUST support creating, listing, accepting, rejecting, and
cancelling invitations via the org plugin, MUST deliver invitation email via
Resend when `RESEND_API_KEY` is set, and MUST fall back to a dev-log stub
(mirroring the existing verification stub) when it is absent.

#### Scenario: Invite sent with Resend configured
- GIVEN RESEND_API_KEY is set and an owner invites user@x.com to org A
- WHEN the invitation is created
- THEN an invitation record is persisted (status pending, expiry set)
- AND the invitation email is sent via Resend

#### Scenario: Invite sent without Resend configured
- GIVEN RESEND_API_KEY is absent
- WHEN an invitation is created
- THEN the invitation record is persisted identically
- AND the email payload is written to the dev-log stub instead of sent

### Requirement: Invited-user registration path
When a user registers with an email matching one or more pending,
unexpired invitations, the system MUST NOT auto-create a personal
organization for that user, and MUST leave `activeOrganizationId` null
until invitation resolution. The post-registration screen MUST list all
matching pending invitations for individual accept/reject. If an
invitation is rejected or expires without any invitation remaining
accepted or pending, the system MUST fall back to auto-creating a personal
organization on the next session or enrichment pass.

#### Scenario: Register with one pending invite
- GIVEN a visitor whose email matches one pending, unexpired invitation
- WHEN they register
- THEN no personal org is auto-created; activeOrganizationId is null
- AND the post-registration screen lists the pending invitation with
  accept/reject actions

#### Scenario: Register with multiple pending invites
- GIVEN a visitor's email matches two pending invitations from different orgs
- WHEN they register
- THEN the post-registration screen lists both invitations independently

#### Scenario: Accept resolves the active org
- GIVEN a user with activeOrganizationId null and a pending invitation
- WHEN they accept it
- THEN they become a member; activeOrganizationId is set to that org

#### Scenario: Reject or expiry falls back to personal org
- GIVEN a user with activeOrganizationId null whose only pending
  invitation is rejected or expires
- WHEN the next session/enrichment pass runs
- THEN a personal org is auto-created and activeOrganizationId is set to it

## Capability: `module-access` (NEW)

### Requirement: Granular module access grants
MUST persist per-member grants in `member_module_access` (member, module,
store nullable = all stores). A member MUST be denied access outside
granted rows unless role is owner/admin.

#### Scenario: Module-restricted member denied outside grant
- GIVEN a member of org A granted `orders` for store S1 only
- WHEN they call orders' public API for store S2
- THEN access is denied

#### Scenario: Owner/admin bypass granular grants
- GIVEN an owner of org A with no explicit grant rows
- WHEN they call any module public API scoped to org A
- THEN access is granted

### Requirement: withOrg() query-scoping contract
MUST provide a single `withOrg()` helper in shared/db scoping every
business query to the session's org. Callable ONLY from a module's
public API (index.ts), never inline route/app code. Every business query
MUST pass through it.

#### Scenario: Query scoped through withOrg()
- GIVEN a module public API function reading tenant data
- WHEN it executes via withOrg(sessionOrgId, cb)
- THEN the query includes an org-id filter matching the session org

### Requirement: Cross-organization isolation
MUST guarantee org A session can never read/write org B's member,
invitation, or member_module_access rows (or any tenant data) via any
exported identity API. isolation.test.ts is the enforcing gate and MUST
be the first artifact written during apply (strict TDD, red-first).

#### Scenario: Org A cannot access org B's members
- GIVEN seeded orgs A and B, each with owner + member
- WHEN an org A session calls any exported identity API for org B's
  members/invitations/module-access
- THEN it returns no org B data (empty or denied)

#### Scenario: Org A cannot write into org B
- GIVEN the same fixture
- WHEN an org A session attempts to create/update/delete an org B
  member/invitation/module-access row
- THEN the write is rejected

## Capability: `abuse-mitigation-mechanism` (NEW)

### Requirement: Verification enforcement infra present, not gating
MUST wire a verification-enforcement toggle for future use, MUST NOT
block any user action on unverified email in V2-01.

#### Scenario: Unverified user unaffected in V2-01
- GIVEN a user with emailVerified false
- WHEN they perform register/invitation-send/other in-scope actions
- THEN no action is blocked due to verification state

### Requirement: Postgres fixed-window rate limiting
MUST rate-limit `register` and `invitation-send` via a `rate_limit_bucket`
table keyed (ip, endpoint, window_start), fixed-window UPSERT increment,
returning HTTP 429 when the window count exceeds the limit.

#### Scenario: Under limit succeeds
- GIVEN fewer requests than limit in current window for (ip, register)
- WHEN another arrives
- THEN it succeeds and the bucket increments

#### Scenario: Over limit returns 429
- GIVEN limit reached for (ip, register) in current window
- WHEN another request arrives same window
- THEN rejected HTTP 429, bucket not incremented

#### Scenario: Window rollover resets the count
- GIVEN limit reached in window W for (ip, invitation-send)
- WHEN a request arrives in window W+1
- THEN a new bucket row starts at count 1 and succeeds

## Capability: `auth-foundation` (MODIFIED)

### Requirement: Registration auto-creates an organization and establishes a session
MUST establish an authenticated session on registration. MUST auto-create
a personal org UNLESS the email matches a pending, unexpired invitation,
in which case org auto-creation is skipped per the invited-user
registration path. Email verification remains not required to complete
this flow.
(Previously: auto-org creation was unconditional on every registration.)

#### Scenario: Register creates org and session (no pending invite)
- GIVEN a visitor with a valid email and no matching pending invitation
- WHEN they register
- THEN a user + auto-created org (owner) + session with
  activeOrganizationId set to it

#### Scenario: Register skips auto-org when a pending invite matches
- GIVEN a visitor's email matches a pending, unexpired invitation
- WHEN they register
- THEN no org is auto-created; activeOrganizationId is null

#### Scenario: Unverified user still has a usable session
- GIVEN a user just registered, email not verified
- WHEN they make an authenticated request immediately after
- THEN it succeeds, no verification-required error

### Requirement: Session carries activeOrganizationId, except while an invitation is pending
MUST carry non-null activeOrganizationId, EXCEPT MAY be null while the
user has at least one unresolved pending invitation and no membership
yet. Once all invitations resolve, the next session/enrichment pass MUST
leave activeOrganizationId non-null.
(Previously: unconditionally non-null after every register/login.)

#### Scenario: Session includes activeOrganizationId after register (no pending invite)
- GIVEN register flow with no matching pending invitation
- WHEN session inspected
- THEN activeOrganizationId present and non-null

#### Scenario: Session includes activeOrganizationId after login
- GIVEN login flow
- WHEN session inspected
- THEN activeOrganizationId present and non-null

#### Scenario: Session tolerates null activeOrganizationId while invite pending
- GIVEN a user registered with a matching pending invitation, unresolved
- WHEN session inspected
- THEN activeOrganizationId is null and no in-scope flow errors on it

### Regression: unchanged auth-foundation behavior
Login, logout, verification hook surface (wired/not enforced), and
migration-created tables remain as in the archived spec.

#### Scenario: V2-00 auth-foundation suite stays green
- GIVEN the V2-00 auth-foundation test suite
- WHEN run after this change is applied
- THEN all previously passing tests remain passing

observations.title: sdd/v2-01-identity/design
observations.content:
# Design: V2-01 Identity (F1, 🔥 HOT — judgment-day required before archive) — rev 2 (validator reconciliation)

> Canonical file: win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-01-identity/design.md (full version with mermaid diagrams). This is the condensed Engram copy. All better-auth facts verified against installed 1.6.23 dist. Rev 2 reconciles 2 CRITICALs + 1 WARNING from the fresh-context validator (spec.md amended in the same pass, orchestrator-authorized).

## Approach
Use better-auth org plugin as-is (invite/accept/reject/cancel/list endpoints, sendInvitationEmail, organizationHooks, setActiveOrganization); build only member_module_access, withOrg(), rate_limit_bucket limiter, shared/email Resend+dev-stub adapter, and the pending-invitation fix in ensureOwnerOrganization. Strict TDD; isolation.test.ts red-first is the gate.

## Decisions
- **D1 orphan-org fix**: pending-invite check INSIDE ensureOwnerOrganization, inside the pg_advisory_xact_lock transaction, after locked membership re-check + email lookup: pending AND unexpired (expires_at > now() in SQL, never trust status alone) AND lower(email) match (better-auth lowercases invite emails: creation path crud-invites.mjs:87, resend payload :153). Found → return [] (skip creation); pickActiveOrganizationId([]) already yields null — no signature change. Rejected: wrapper (TOCTOU outside lock), hook-level check. Residual accepted race: expiry boundary between accept-validation and our check → fallback org + accepted membership (benign, no orphan-only state).
- **D2 null activeOrganizationId**: means "membership unresolved". Guard in src/app/dashboard/layout.tsx (server) → redirect /invitations. Accept action → acceptInvitation + setActiveOrganization; reject action → if 0 remaining pending + 0 memberships → ensureOwnerOrganization + setActiveOrganization. All-expired handled lazily on /invitations load. Rejected: Next middleware (edge, no pooled PG), cron.
- **D3 withOrg()**: shared/db/with-org.ts — `withOrg<T>(orgId, fn(scope): Promise<T>)`; scope = { orgId, db, filter(table, extra?) → and(eq(table.organizationId, orgId), extra), values(table, row) force-injecting organizationId }. Throws on falsy orgId. Enforcement: eslint-plugin-boundaries (app/** imports only modules/*/index.ts; shared/db only from modules/* + shared/{auth,seed}); withOrg is NOT re-exported from any module public API, and an explicit no-restricted-imports (or boundaries) rule bars withOrg imports from app/** and worker/** — modules only. Behavioral backstop: isolation.test.ts. Rejected: repo pattern (fork B), Postgres RLS (pool conflicts), AsyncLocalStorage.
- **D4 member_module_access**: id PK, organization_id FK cascade, member_id FK cascade, module NOT NULL, store_id NULL (=all stores; no FK yet), uniqueIndex(member_id, module, store_id).nullsNotDistinct(). Resolution resolveModuleAccess (exported ONLY from modules/identity/index.ts): owner|admin → allow all; member → module-wide row (store_id NULL) → allow; exact store row → allow; else DENY (deny-by-default; zero rows = no access). Rejected: allow-by-default, resolution in shared/auth.
- **D5 invitations**: better-auth endpoints verbatim (accept requires session — confirmed, drives D1); identity-module server actions wrap for UI only. sendInvitationEmail → new src/shared/email/send-email.ts: RESEND_API_KEY → resend SDK, else dev log stub (URL only in development, mirrors logVerificationEmailStub). Resend-invite: invite-member resend:true extends expiresAt + re-fires email (crud-invites.mjs:146-154). 48h default expiry kept.
- **D6 rate limiting**: rate_limit_bucket(key, window_start, count, PK(key,window_start)); consumeRateLimit: fixed window floor(epoch/windowSeconds), atomic INSERT..ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE count+1 RETURNING; lazy sampled cleanup (2 windows). Integration: global options.hooks.before (verified api/dispatch.mjs:139) matching /sign-up/email (key register:{ip}) and /organization/invite-member (key invite:{userId}). KEYING (deliberate deviation from naive uniform IP keying; spec amended to match): register is unauthenticated → client IP is the only stable key; invitation-send is authenticated → throttle the principal (userId), not the NAT-shared network location. INCREMENT SEMANTICS (spec aligned): UPSERT increments unconditionally even over limit — observably irrelevant in a fixed window (429 persists until rollover either way) and the single unconditional statement is what keeps the limiter atomic; spec asserts only the observable (429 while over limit within window, allowed after rollover). Over limit → APIError TOO_MANY_REQUESTS → 429 {code: RATE_LIMITED, retryAfter}. IP: x-forwarded-for first hop, fallback "unknown" shared bucket. Rejected: better-auth built-in rateLimit (customStorage is non-atomic get/set; activates global default rules; rolling window ≠ settled fixed window), Next middleware (misses auth.api calls).
- **D7 verification**: env REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION (default false) → emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification; real email via shared/email. Mechanism only; policy V2-02.
- **D8 UI**: /invitations page; dashboard/layout.tsx guard; dashboard/settings/organization (name/slug); dashboard/settings/members (members table, invite form, two-level role editor: simple dropdown ⇄ module×store matrix). All data via modules/identity public API.

## Files
Modify: ensure-owner-organization.ts (highest risk), auth.ts, env, modules/identity/index.ts (members/invitations/resolveModuleAccess APIs — NO withOrg re-export per D3), boundaries config. Create: shared/db/{with-org,rate-limit}.ts, schema/{module-access,rate-limit}.ts + 2 additive migrations, shared/email/send-email.ts, app/invitations/*, dashboard/layout.tsx, dashboard/settings/*, seed second-org-invited-member step.

## Testing
Isolation FIRST (red, real PG, two seeded orgs; module-restricted member denied outside grant). Unit: pending-invite check (FakeTx, expiry boundary, lowercase), resolveModuleAccess matrix, limiter window/consume, email adapter selection. Integration (real PG): invite→register→no orphan→accept; reject-last→fallback org; concurrent UPSERT. E2E: invite flow incl. dev-stub capture; 429 burst.

## Rollout
Additive migrations only, droppable. Stacked PRs (800-line budget), feature branch chain: Slice 1 = schemas + migrations + withOrg + boundaries + seed fixtures + isolation.test.ts; Slice 2 = D1 fix + null-org flow + invitations + email + /invitations UI; Slice 3 = limiter + verification toggle + settings/members UI + E2E.

## Threat matrix
N/A — no shell/subprocess/VCS/PR-automation/executable-classification boundary.

## Spec reconciliation (rev 2, orchestrator-authorized spec edits)
- spec Requirement "Postgres fixed-window rate limiting": key now register→client IP, invitation-send→authenticated user id (was uniform (ip, endpoint, window_start)).
- spec "Over limit returns 429" scenario: dropped "bucket is not incremented" (implementation detail); asserts only 429 persistence within the window; rollover scenario key updated to (userId, invitation-send).

## Open questions
None blocking. HOT change: flag judgment-day (2 blind judges) before archive per config rules.

observations.title: Atributos de embarcación (INMARSAT/satelital/arte de pesca) deben precargarse desde la embarcación en Validación
observations.content:
**What (hallazgo del usuario en auditoría VM)**: En Validación, INMARSAT, "¿tiene equipo satelital?" y "arte de pesca" se muestran como campos manuales/fijos, pero son atributos de la EMBARCACIÓN y deben venir precargados de ella.

**Diagnóstico**: en `frontend/src/lib/acopio-validation.ts` buildInitialValues: `arte_pesca` se prellena con `config.defaultFishingMethod` (FIJO por tenant, línea 250); `inmarsat` se lee de `asset_metadata.inmarsat` (línea 249) pero el valor real está en la COLUMNA `acopio_intake_assets.inmarsat`. El arrival asset solo expone `ia.metadata AS asset_metadata`, NO las columnas reales (inmarsat/has_satellite_equipment/satellite_equipment_detail de migración 023). NO existe columna arte_pesca. Al guardar, todo va a aa.metadata por-llegada.

**Decisión del usuario**: arte de pesca SÍ sale de PRODUCE (confirmado con captura: campo "ARTE PESCA" ej. "T. ARTES Y APAREJOS" + REGIMEN "ARTESANAL" en la búsqueda de Embarcaciones Pesqueras). Guardarlo asociado a la embarcación en acopio_intake_assets porque cada embarcación varía.

**Plan en curso**: Backend (agente): migración 039 arte_pesca en acopio_intake_assets; extraer arte de pesca de PRODUCE en parseProduceHtml/vessel-sync (investigar si está en _datosEmbarcacion/{id} o solo en la búsqueda); exponer inmarsat/has_satellite_equipment/satellite_equipment_detail/arte_pesca en el arrival asset. Frontend (pendiente): prellenar los 3 desde la embarcación en Validación en vez de config default/metadata.

**Relacionado no resuelto**: la data descriptiva del PERMISO_PESCA (numero_permiso, representante, etc.) NO se ve en Validación porque el entity_document de permiso del portal solo guarda vigencia+autorizacion, no ai_extracted_json con campos curados (el LibraryDocEditor de #2a no tiene qué mostrar). observations.title: Endpoint PRODUCE buscador de embarcaciones (arte de pesca) — reverse-engineered
observations.content:
**What**: Endpoint del buscador de embarcaciones de PRODUCE que expone el ARTE DE PESCA (no está en la ficha `_datosEmbarcacion` que scrapeamos hoy).

**Flujo**:
1. GET `https://consultasenlinea.produce.gob.pe/ConsultasEnLinea/consultas.web/embarcacion` con cookie jar → extraer token del HTML: `<input id="token" name="token" type="hidden" value="<128-hex>"/>`. Token por page-load, atado a la cookie de sesión.
2. POST `https://consultasenlinea.produce.gob.pe/ConsultasEnLinea/consultas.web/ajax/listado.embarcaciones.ajax.php` (form-urlencoded, misma cookie, Referer = página base) con: `tipBusqueda=2` (MATRÍCULA), `desNombre=<matrícula MAYÚSCULAS>`, `arte=0 regimen=0 preserva=0 casco=0 destino=0 estado=0 zarpe=0 idConvenio=0 idNominada=0`, `token=<token>`, y DataTables `sEcho=1 iColumns=7 iDisplayStart=0 iDisplayLength=20 sSearch=`.
3. Respuesta JSON: `{"aaData":[["30455"," CH. JHOCIMAR","IO-30455-BM","OLGA CHANA MAMANI","T. ARTES Y APAREJOS ","ARTESANAL","MADERA","TODO EL LITORAL","VIGENTE","NO"]]}`. Índices aaData[i]: [0]=id [1]=nombre [2]=matrícula [3]=armador [4]=ARTE PESCA [5]=régimen [6]=casco [7]=zona [8]=estado.

**Uso**: arte de pesca = aaData[fila][4].trim(). IDENTITY GUARD obligatorio: elegir la fila cuyo [2] (matrícula normalizada) == la consultada; si ninguna, null (no tomar fila 0 a ciegas — evita el bug histórico de asociar data ajena).

**Verificado con curl -k** (cert vencido) desde local. Cert vencido → el backend ya usa un agente node:https custom (ver dicapiRaw). Se implementó en registry-sync.fetchVesselArtePesca + vessel-sync (migración 039 arte_pesca). Ver [[atributos-de-embarcaci-n-inmarsat-satelital-arte-de-pesca-deben-precargarse-desde-la-embarcaci-n-en]].

**Bonus disponible (no usado aún)**: régimen [5] (ARTESANAL), casco [6], zona [7] también vienen — si se quieren, agregar columnas.

## Exploration: v2-02-billing

### Current State

**Repo**: win_comerce_v1 (branch v2-01/slice-3, tip 3cee396). `src/modules/` has one module so far: `identity` (public API via `src/modules/identity/index.ts`, internal helpers not exported). No `billing` module dir exists yet.

**Org/session context**: `src/shared/auth/auth.ts` — better-auth 1.6.23 + `organization` plugin, Drizzle adapter, `ipAddressHeaders: []` (proxy-less deployment, per-IP rate limiting is best-effort until F6 proxy lands). `session.activeOrganizationId` is guaranteed non-null once a session exists (`session.create.before` calls `ensureOwnerOrganization`). `getSession(headers)` (`src/shared/auth/session.ts`) is the read path; `src/modules/identity/index.ts` re-exports `getSession`, `getActiveOrganization`, `getActiveMemberRole`.

**withOrg() — the mandatory chokepoint** (`src/shared/db/with-org.ts`):
```ts
export function withOrg<T>(orgId: string, fn: (scope: OrgScope) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
// scope.filter(table, extra?) -> and(eq(table.organizationId, orgId), extra?)
// scope.values(table, row) -> { ...row, organizationId: orgId }
```
Throws synchronously on falsy/whitespace orgId. Callable ONLY from a module's `index.ts` — statically enforced by eslint-boundaries + `no-restricted-imports` (bars `app/**`/`worker/**`). Every new `credit_movement`/`subscription`/`plans`/`tool_cost` table with `organizationId` MUST be queried exclusively through this. Behavioral backstop pattern: `with-org.isolation.test.ts` (real Postgres, `describe.runIf(!!MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL)`, seeds two orgs via `seedOrgWithOwnerAndMember`, asserts cross-org query returns zero rows). V2-02 needs an equivalent isolation test for the ledger/subscription tables (multitenant-isolation spec rule).

**Drizzle schema conventions** (`src/shared/db/schema/{auth,module-access,rate-limit}.ts`, aggregated in `schema/index.ts`):
- `text("id").primaryKey()` with app-generated `randomBytes(16).toString("hex")` ids (no serial/uuid column type — plain text, generated in app code, see `ensure-owner-organization.ts`/`module-access-grants.ts`).
- `organizationId: text(...).notNull().references(() => organization.id, { onDelete: "cascade" })` + a dedicated `index("<table>_organizationId_idx")`.
- Timestamps: `timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull()` (or `.notNull()` without default when the app always supplies it, as in `member`/`invitation`); `updatedAt` uses `$onUpdate(() => new Date())` where mutation happens.
- Multi-column app-level uniqueness leads with `organizationId` (Fix 2b lesson from V2-01 judgment-day: leading org-scope column prevents cross-tenant collision DoS) and uses `.nullsNotDistinct()` where a nullable dimension (like `storeId`) must still count toward uniqueness.
- `relations()` blocks co-located per table for Drizzle's relational query API.

**Append-only ledger precedent already in the codebase**: `rate_limit_bucket` (`src/shared/db/schema/rate-limit.ts` + `src/shared/db/rate-limit.ts`) is a fixed-window counter table using an atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1 RETURNING count` — good reference for "atomic increment under concurrency" but it is NOT append-only (single row per window, mutated). The ROADMAP explicitly wants `credit_movement` append-only with `balance = SUM(...)`, closer in spirit to the planned V2-12 `stock_movement` append-only pattern (same "saldo = suma" phrasing) — no existing append-only-ledger code to copy directly; V2-02 is the first of this family.

**Concurrency/locking precedent — directly reusable**: `ensure-owner-organization.ts` uses `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(${key})::bigint)` inside `db.transaction()` for a check-then-insert race (a stable, well-documented, already-reviewed pattern in this codebase, including a documented duck-typed `23505` unique-violation retry helper). This is the strongest candidate mechanism for `consumeCredits` concurrency safety (see Approaches below).

**better-auth email verification hook** (verified against installed `node_modules/better-auth/dist/api/routes/email-verification.mjs`): `ctx.context.options.emailVerification.afterEmailVerification(updatedUser, request)` fires right after `emailVerified` flips to `true` in the DB (both the OTP-less and change-email-verification flows call it). This is NOT currently wired in `auth.ts` (only `sendVerificationEmail` is set). It is the correct hook to gate trial-credit grant per Trap #11's "verification obligatoria antes de otorgar créditos de trial". `requireEmailVerification` in `emailAndPassword` (currently `env.REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION`, defaults false per V2-01 D7) is a separate, orthogonal toggle — gating login, not credits.

**1-trial-per-email**: no existing table encodes this. `user.email` is already `unique()` (schema/auth.ts), so "1 trial per verified email" is naturally enforced if trial-grant is keyed off `userId`/`user.email` with a uniqueness constraint on a new table (e.g. `credit_movement` row with `type = 'grant_plan'`/a dedicated `trial_grant` marker) rather than re-derivable state. Needs an explicit unique index (e.g. on `(userId)` in a small `trial_grant` marker table, or a partial unique index on `credit_movement` where `reason = 'trial'`), following the same "app check + DB constraint as defense in depth" doubled pattern used for `member_organizationId_userId_uidx` / `member_module_access` uniqueness.

**Admin UI / settings pattern** (`src/app/dashboard/settings/organization/page.tsx`, `.../members/page.tsx` + `role-editor.tsx`): Next.js Server Component reads session via `getSession(headers())`, redirects to `/login` or `/invitations` if unauthenticated/no active org, calls a module's public API function, renders a form with a `"use server"` action calling back into the module API, then `redirect()`s. Billing admin screens (manual plan activation, manual top-up recording, tool-cost editing) should follow this exact shape, calling a new `billing` module's `index.ts` exports — never `withOrg` directly from `app/**`.

**`member_module_access` and billing UI gating**: `memberModuleAccess` (module string, nullable `storeId`) is a generic per-module grant table already used to gate other modules per member. Whether billing UI/consumption is gated by it is an OPEN QUESTION — V2-01 built the mechanism generically ("orders" was the example module in the isolation test), but nothing in V2-01 wires billing specifically. Design choice for V2-02: either (a) billing/subscription settings are owner/admin-only by role (`isElevatedRole`, already exported from identity) and NOT run through `memberModuleAccess` at all, or (b) `consumeCredits` execution paths for a *tool* respect `memberModuleAccess` for that tool's owning module. Recommend (a) for the admin/settings surface (mirrors `organization`/`members` settings, which are role-gated, not module-access-gated) and defer (b) to whichever module actually calls `consumeCredits` (V2-05 pipeline-agentes) — V2-02 only needs to expose `consumeCredits(org, tool)` and let callers decide access.

### Affected Areas (new code, no existing files touched — this is greenfield within the repo)
- `win_comerce_v1/src/shared/db/schema/billing.ts` (new) — `subscription`, `plans`, `credit_movement`, `tool_cost` tables, following the org-scoped/index/relations conventions above.
- `win_comerce_v1/src/shared/db/schema/index.ts` — must re-export the new schema file (aggregation point, like `module-access.ts` is already wired in).
- `win_comerce_v1/src/modules/billing/` (new module) — `index.ts` public API (mirrors `modules/identity/index.ts`), internal implementation files (`consume-credits.ts`, `subscriptions.ts`, `plans.ts`, `payment-gateway.ts` interface + a `manual` implementation for V2-02).
- `win_comerce_v1/src/shared/auth/auth.ts` — needs `emailVerification.afterEmailVerification` wired to call the billing module's trial-grant function (module boundary: this is `shared/auth` calling into a module's public API — same shape as how `auth.ts` already calls `ensureOwnerOrganization` from `shared/auth`, so a billing module export imported here should be fine, but must go through eslint-boundaries check since `shared/auth` is not `app/**`/`worker/**`).
- `win_comerce_v1/src/app/dashboard/settings/billing/` (new) — admin plan activation / top-up recording UI, following the `settings/organization` page pattern.
- `win_comerce_v1/src/shared/db/with-org.isolation.test.ts` or a new `credit-movement.isolation.test.ts` — cross-org isolation coverage for the new tenant-data tables (mandatory per multitenant-isolation spec rule).
- `win_comerce_v1/src/shared/seed/factories.ts` / `steps/` — likely needs a billing seed step (plans data, a demo subscription) mirroring `demo-org-owner.ts`/`second-org-invited-member.ts`.

### Portable ideas from v1 (`/home/rodrigo/Documentos/trabajos/ecomerce/win-comerce`, NOT the broken `win_comerce_link` symlink)

v1 billing is real but thin — Stripe checkout + webhook + counter-based usage, not a credit ledger:
- `functions/api/webhook/stripe.ts` — parses `checkout.session.completed`/`.expired`/`payment_intent.payment_failed`/`customer.subscription.deleted`, verifies `Stripe-Signature` via raw Web Crypto HMAC-SHA256 (portable idea: manual HMAC verification without the Stripe SDK, since v1 ran on Cloudflare Workers). **Idempotency gap** (relevant to Trap #4): the only guard against double-processing is checking `tx.payment_status === 'completed'` before mutating — there is NO unique constraint on the Stripe event id itself, so a genuinely duplicate delivery with a still-`pending` local transaction row could double-process. V2-02's `PaymentGateway` interface should design in a real `UNIQUE` external-event-id + upsert from day one (per Trap #4 and per the ROADMAP's own §4.4 explicit requirement), not repeat this gap even though v1's manual v1-of-module has no live webhook yet.
- `migrations/0003_crm_users_plans.sql` — v1's `plans`/`subscriptions`/`usage_counters` shape: plans carry `agent_limits_json` (feature/limit blob) and `price_usd`; subscriptions are mutable single-row-per-user with `status` enum (`active|past_due|canceled|trialing`) and `current_period_start/end`. This mutable-row-per-user subscription shape (not append-only) is reasonable to port AS-IS for the new `subscription` table (1/org) — the ROADMAP only mandates append-only for the *credit ledger*, not the subscription row itself.
- `functions/api/user/usage.ts` — simple counter read, no credits; V2-02 replaces this whole model with `consumeCredits`+ledger, so usage_counters is not portable, just useful as a "what NOT to repeat" reference (counters can drift/reset incorrectly; ledger SUM cannot).
- No trial-credit-gated-by-email-verification logic exists in v1 at all — confirms Trap #11's trial-credit split is new work for v2, not a port.

### Approaches — key design questions

**1. Ledger balance strategy**
1. **SUM-on-read** — `balance = SUM(amount) FROM credit_movement WHERE organizationId = ?` computed on every read.
   - Pros: correctness by construction (no drift possible), matches the ROADMAP's own "saldo = suma" phrasing verbatim, matches the append-only `stock_movement` pattern planned for V2-12 (consistency across the codebase), no extra invalidation logic.
   - Cons: read cost grows with row count per org over the product's lifetime; needs `index (organizationId, createdAt)` at minimum.
   - Effort: Low.
2. **Materialized balance column + ledger** — a `subscription.creditBalance` (or dedicated `credit_balance` table) column updated transactionally alongside each `credit_movement` insert.
   - Pros: O(1) balance reads, cheaper at scale.
   - Cons: two writes must stay in sync (balance update + ledger insert) inside one transaction, reintroduces exactly the "materialized state can drift from the source of truth" risk the ROADMAP is explicitly avoiding by mandating append-only; adds a second race condition surface instead of removing one.
   - Effort: Medium.

**Recommendation**: SUM-on-read for V2-02. Ledger tables in this domain (rate-limit bucket aside) are small per org relative to typical read volume; if performance becomes an issue later, a periodic checkpoint/snapshot row (still auditable, not authoritative) can be added without changing the ledger's append-only contract — that's a reversible future optimization, not a day-1 requirement. This also directly satisfies "race-condition test required" more simply: a SUM-based balance is trivially correct once inserts are guarded (see next question), with no separate balance-column race to test.

**2. `consumeCredits(org, tool)` concurrency**

Since the ledger is append-only, there's no natural row to `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` — the balance is a derived aggregate, not a row. Two viable approaches, both must run "debit BEFORE executing the tool, never after" per the ROADMAP:
1. **`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(orgId)::bigint)`** inside a `db.transaction()`: acquire the org-scoped lock, `SELECT SUM(amount)` for current balance, `SELECT cost FROM tool_cost WHERE tool = ?`, if `balance >= cost` insert a `consumption` row (negative amount) and commit; else throw/return insufficient-funds. This is the exact pattern already reviewed and battle-tested in `ensure-owner-organization.ts` (same `hashtext(...)::bigint` idiom) — reusing it keeps the codebase consistent and lets the tasks/design phase point to prior art instead of inventing a new locking primitive.
   - Pros: proven in this codebase, holds the lock only for the duration of one transaction, naturally serializes concurrent `consumeCredits` calls for the same org (which is exactly the desired race-safety boundary — a different org's calls are never blocked).
   - Cons: advisory locks are session/transaction-scoped and must be paired correctly with the pool (already handled correctly in the existing helper — same connection must run the lock and the queries).
   - Effort: Low (pattern copy + adapt).
2. **Postgres `SERIALIZABLE` isolation** on the transaction instead of an explicit lock, retrying on serialization failure (`40001`).
   - Pros: no explicit lock key management.
   - Cons: needs a retry loop for serialization failures (new failure-handling code not yet present anywhere else in the codebase), harder to reason about under load, and the advisory-lock approach is already precedented and reviewed here.
   - Effort: Medium.

**Recommendation**: Advisory lock (option 1), directly modeled on `ensure-owner-organization.ts`. This is also naturally where "debit before execution" is enforced structurally: `consumeCredits` is a synchronous precondition function whose transaction must commit before the caller is allowed to invoke the tool; callers never call the tool inside the locked transaction (keep external I/O out of the lock's critical section, matching the existing helper's "avoid holding a transaction+lock across app-layer calls to other subsystems" lesson, res-3 in that file's comments, which specifically warns against calling out to another connection-holding subsystem while inside a transaction).

**3. `PaymentGateway` interface shape (webhook-ready even though v1 is manual)**

Design the interface now so a real gateway (Mercado Pago / Lemon Squeezy / Culqi — undecided) can implement it later without reshaping callers:
```ts
interface PaymentGateway {
  createTopUpIntent(input: { orgId: string; credits: number; amountCents: number }): Promise<{ externalRef: string; redirectUrl?: string }>;
  handleWebhookEvent(input: { externalEventId: string; payload: unknown; signatureHeader?: string }): Promise<WebhookResult>; // idempotent — same externalEventId processed twice is a no-op
}
```
The `manual` V2-02 implementation of this interface is a thin admin-triggered function (admin records a top-up = calls the same code path a webhook would call, with a synthetic/admin-generated `externalEventId`) — this is exactly what makes it "webhook-ready": the manual path and the future webhook path converge on one idempotent apply-topup function keyed by a UNIQUE `externalEventId`/`(gateway, externalEventId)` constraint on whatever table records applied top-ups (a `credit_movement` row of `type = 'topup'` with a unique external-id column, or a separate `payment_event` table with a UNIQUE index that the ledger insert references). This directly satisfies Trap #4.

**4. Trial-credit grant flow tied to `emailVerified`**

Wire `emailVerification.afterEmailVerification` in `auth.ts` to call a new billing module export (e.g. `grantTrialCreditsIfEligible(userId)`), which: checks the user has no prior trial grant (unique constraint per question above), resolves the user's org via existing `ensureOwnerOrganization`/membership lookup, and inserts a `credit_movement` row of `type = 'grant_plan'` (or a distinct `trial` reason) inside the same advisory-lock/transaction pattern as `consumeCredits` (same org-scoped lock — grant and consume share the same race-safety boundary). Must follow the "never rethrow, report to Sentry" pattern already used for other after-hooks (`handleUserCreateAfter`) since better-auth after-hooks running post-commit should not fail the verification request itself.

**5. Plans-as-data seeding**

Follow the existing `src/shared/seed/steps/*.ts` pattern (`demo-org-owner.ts`, `second-org-invited-member.ts`) — a new seed step inserts the initial `plans` rows (tiered top-up credit price per plan) and is composed into `runner.ts`. Admin-editable means a `plans` table (not hardcoded config), consistent with the ROADMAP's explicit "planes como data editable por admin."

### Open product questions for the proposal phase to surface to the owner

- Exact plan tiers and top-up credit prices per tier (v1 had free/starter/growth/pro at $0/$19/$49/$99 — is this the intended v2 pricing, or all-new?).
- Which payment gateway is finally decided (Mercado Pago / Lemon Squeezy / Culqi) — affects only the concrete `PaymentGateway` implementation, not the interface, but the proposal should note it's still open per the ROADMAP.
- Trial credit amount and expiry policy (does trial credit expire, or is it a permanent grant consumable at any time?).
- Whether `member_module_access` should gate the billing/settings UI itself, or only role (owner/admin) — recommended in this exploration to use role-only gating for the settings surface, deferring module-access gating to whichever module later calls `consumeCredits` for a specific tool.
- Whether `tool_cost` costs vary by plan tier (ROADMAP only says "tiered top-up credit price per plan", not tiered tool cost) — assume tool cost is plan-independent (flat cost per tool in credits) unless the owner says otherwise.

### Risks
- Ledger SUM-on-read performance at scale is unvalidated — acceptable for V2-02 given current data volumes, but proposal/design should note it as a documented future optimization, not silently ignore it.
- `emailVerification.afterEmailVerification` wiring in `auth.ts` crosses from `shared/auth` into a new `billing` module's public API — must be verified against eslint-boundaries config before assuming it's allowed (identity's own module already imports FROM shared/auth the other direction; the reverse direction, shared calling into a module, needs an explicit boundaries check in design/apply, not assumed here).
- No existing precedent in this codebase for a `PaymentGateway`-style external-service interface abstraction — the shape proposed here is new and should get explicit review (this is exactly the kind of decision the HOT 🔥 judgment-day gate exists for).
- 1-trial-per-email enforcement needs a concrete unique constraint decided in design (not just app-level checking) — flagged but not fully specified here; design phase must pick the exact table/column.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes. The codebase conventions (withOrg, schema shape, advisory-lock concurrency pattern, module public-API boundary, settings-page pattern, better-auth hook surface) are well-understood and directly reusable. The open product questions above (pricing, gateway choice, trial amount/expiry, module-access gating scope) should be explicitly called out in the proposal for owner confirmation before design commits to specifics.

observations.title: sdd/v2-02-billing/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: V2-02 Billing (F1, 🔥 HOT)

> ROADMAP.md §3 F1 (change V2-02), traps #4 (webhook idempotency) and #11 (trial-credit abuse, policy half). Judgment-day (2 blind judges) required before archive. Baseline: v2-01/slice-3 (V2-01 archived). Canonical file: win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-02-billing/proposal.md

## Intent

Monetization and credit-metering foundation: every paid feature from V2-05 onward must debit credits BEFORE execution. v1 used drift-prone usage counters and had a real webhook idempotency gap (explore: no unique Stripe event id). V2-02 ships an append-only credit ledger (balance = SUM), a swappable webhook-ready `PaymentGateway`, and closes Trap #11's policy half: trial credits gated by verified email, one trial per email.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Schema `billing.ts`: `subscription` (1/org, mutable status row), `plans` (admin-editable data incl. tiered top-up credit price per plan), `credit_movement` (append-only: grant_plan | topup | consumption | adjustment), `tool_cost` (editable). All org-scoped tables exclusively via `withOrg()`.
- `modules/billing` public API: `consumeCredits(org, tool)` (debit before tool execution), plan activation, top-up recording, balance read.
- `PaymentGateway` interface, idempotent by `UNIQUE (gateway, externalEventId)`; V2-02 implementation = `manual` (admin-triggered, synthetic event id).
- Trial credits: `afterEmailVerification` hook → `grantTrialCreditsIfEligible`; 1-trial-per-verified-email DB constraint; never-rethrow hook pattern.
- Admin UI (settings-page pattern, owner/admin only): plan activation, top-up recording, tool-cost editing.
- Seed step: plans + demo subscription. Isolation test + concurrency race test.

### Out of Scope
- Real payment gateway integration (interface only); `consumeCredits` callers (V2-05+); per-IP hardening (F6); credit expiry, refunds, chargebacks.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `billing-plans`: subscription lifecycle (1/org), plans-as-data, admin plan activation.
- `credit-ledger`: append-only `credit_movement`, SUM balance, `consumeCredits` debit-before-execution, `tool_cost`.
- `payment-gateway`: swappable interface, external-event-id idempotency contract, manual implementation.
- `trial-credits`: emailVerified-gated grant, one per verified email (Trap #11 policy atop V2-01 mechanism).

### Modified Capabilities
- None (`abuse-mitigation-mechanism` stays mechanism-only; the policy lives in `trial-credits`).

## Approach

Adopt exploration recommendations: (1) SUM-on-read ledger with `(organizationId, createdAt)` index — correct by construction; checkpoint row is a reversible future optimization; (2) `consumeCredits` inside `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(orgId))` transaction (pattern proven in `ensure-owner-organization.ts`): lock → SUM → `tool_cost` → insert negative row or insufficient-funds error; transaction commits before the caller may run the tool; (3) manual gateway converges on the same idempotent apply-topup path a webhook will use; (4) trial grant wired via `afterEmailVerification`. Strict TDD; isolation and race tests written red-first.

## Assumptions (pending owner confirmation)

1. Plan tiers seeded with v1 shape (free/starter/growth/pro) as placeholder data; exact prices are admin-editable data, not schema.
2. Concrete gateway choice (Mercado Pago / Lemon Squeezy / Culqi) stays open; only interface + manual implementation ship.
3. Trial credits are a permanent grant (no expiry); amount lives in plans data (exploration default).
4. Billing settings UI gated by role only (owner/admin), NOT `member_module_access`.
5. `tool_cost` is flat per tool, plan-independent.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `src/shared/db/schema/billing.ts` + `index.ts` | New | Four billing tables + migrations |
| `src/modules/billing/*` | New | Public API, consume-credits, plans, payment-gateway |
| `src/shared/auth/auth.ts` | Modified | Wire `afterEmailVerification` → trial grant |
| `src/app/dashboard/settings/billing/*` | New | Admin screens (settings-page pattern) |
| `src/shared/seed/*` | Modified | Plans + demo subscription step |
| billing isolation + race tests | New | Mandatory gates |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrent consumption overdraws balance | Med | Advisory-lock tx + red-first race test |
| Duplicate top-up applied twice (Trap #4) | Med | `UNIQUE (gateway, externalEventId)` from day one |
| Trial farming via re-verification (Trap #11) | Med | DB unique constraint + emailVerified gate |
| `shared/auth` → billing import direction violates boundaries | Med | Explicit eslint-boundaries verification in design |
| SUM-on-read cost at scale | Low | Documented future checkpoint optimization |

## Rollback Plan

Single change branch → revert PR. Migrations additive (four tables droppable). `afterEmailVerification` unhook is a pure code revert. No production data (ROADMAP decision #1).

## Dependencies

- Stacked on archived V2-01 (org identity, `withOrg()`, verified-email + rate-limit mechanisms). ROADMAP §2 graph.
- Enables V2-05 pipeline credit checks and a later real-gateway change.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Isolation test green: org A can never read or affect org B's ledger/subscription (acceptance gate).
- [ ] Race test green: N concurrent `consumeCredits` never overdraw; balance = SUM exact (acceptance gate).
- [ ] Debit-before-execution is structural: consumption row committed before the tool may run.
- [ ] Duplicate external event id (manual or webhook) applies exactly once.
- [ ] Second verification of the same email grants no second trial (DB-enforced).
- [ ] verify PASS, then judgment-day (2 blind judges) PASS before archive.

observations.title: V2-02 product round: v1-style plans seed, permanent trial, role-only UI, tool_cost PER PLAN
observations.content:
**What**: Owner confirmed the V2-02 billing product assumptions (2026-07-20), with ONE deviation from the proposal's recommended defaults:
1. Plans seed data: v1 shape (free/starter/growth/pro at $0/$19/$49/$99) as admin-editable starting point. CONFIRMED default.
2. Trial credits: permanent grant, no expiry; amount as plans data; 1 trial per verified email still enforced. CONFIRMED default.
3. Billing settings UI gating: role-only (owner/admin via isElevatedRole), NOT member_module_access. CONFIRMED default.
4. **tool_cost: PER PLAN (override)** — tool credit cost varies by plan tier, NOT flat. This supersedes proposal Assumption 5. Data model needs a plan dimension on tool cost (e.g. cost per (tool, plan) or base cost + per-plan override), decided in design.
5. Payment gateway concrete choice remains open (interface + manual implementation only in V2-02) — unchanged.

**Why**: SDD product round before spec/design commit to specifics (same flow as V2-01's product round).
**Where**: openspec/changes/v2-02-billing/proposal.md Assumptions section updated by orchestrator to reflect confirmation + override; spec and design phases receive this as authoritative input.
**Learned**: Owner wants pricing power per tier on BOTH axes: top-up credit price per plan (ROADMAP) AND tool execution cost per plan (this decision).

observations.title: sdd/v2-02-billing/spec
observations.content:
# Spec Delta: v2-02-billing

> Source: proposal.md. New capabilities: `billing-plans`, `credit-ledger`,
> `payment-gateway`, `trial-credits`. Modified: `auth-foundation` (hook now
> dispatches trial-credit grant, non-blocking). Multitenant isolation
> scenario included per config.yaml `rules.specs`.
> Full canonical file: win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-02-billing/spec.md

## Capability: `billing-plans` (NEW)

### Requirement: Plans as admin-editable data
The system MUST store plan tiers (free/starter/growth/pro seed) as rows in a
`plans` table, editable by owner/admin, including per-plan top-up credit
price (tiered — better plan is cheaper per credit) and per-plan tool costs.
No plan pricing or tool-cost values MAY be hardcoded in application code.

#### Scenario: Admin edits a plan's top-up price
- GIVEN an authenticated owner/admin
- WHEN they update the top-up credit price for the `pro` plan
- THEN the new price applies to subsequent top-up calculations without a
  deploy

#### Scenario: Better plan yields cheaper top-up credits
- GIVEN `starter` and `pro` plans both active
- WHEN their top-up credit prices are compared
- THEN `pro`'s price per credit is lower than `starter`'s

### Requirement: One subscription per organization, manually activated
The system MUST maintain exactly one mutable `subscription` row per
organization (status: active/past_due/canceled/trialing). Plan activation
MUST be an explicit admin (owner/admin) action; no automatic upgrade/
downgrade occurs in V2-02.

#### Scenario: Admin activates a plan
- GIVEN an org with no active subscription
- WHEN an owner/admin activates the `growth` plan
- THEN the org's single subscription row is set to `active` on `growth`

#### Scenario: Second activation updates, not duplicates
- GIVEN an org already subscribed to `starter`
- WHEN an admin activates `pro`
- THEN the same subscription row is updated to `pro`, no second row exists

## Capability: `credit-ledger` (NEW)

### Requirement: Append-only credit ledger, balance by SUM
The system MUST record every credit change as an immutable
`credit_movement` row (`grant_plan | topup | consumption | adjustment`).
An org's balance MUST always equal `SUM(amount)` over its movements — no
mutable counter is permitted. All ledger queries MUST go through
`withOrg()`.

#### Scenario: Balance reflects the sum of movements
- GIVEN an org with movements +100 (grant_plan), +50 (topup), -20
  (consumption)
- WHEN its balance is read
- THEN the result is 130

### Requirement: Debit-before-execution with per-plan tool cost
`consumeCredits(org, tool)` MUST resolve the tool's credit cost for the
org's active plan, then commit a negative `consumption` movement inside a
transaction BEFORE the caller is permitted to run the tool. Insufficient
balance MUST reject with no movement written and the tool MUST NOT run.

#### Scenario: Sufficient balance debits before execution
- GIVEN an org with balance 50 and a tool costing 10 credits on its plan
- WHEN `consumeCredits` is called
- THEN a -10 movement commits and only then may the tool execute

#### Scenario: Insufficient balance blocks execution
- GIVEN an org with balance 5 and a tool costing 10 credits
- WHEN `consumeCredits` is called
- THEN it rejects with an insufficient-funds error, no movement is written,
  and the tool does not execute

#### Scenario: Tool cost varies by plan
- GIVEN the same tool costs 10 credits on `starter` and 6 on `pro`
- WHEN two orgs on those plans each call `consumeCredits` for that tool
- THEN each is debited its own plan's resolved cost

### Requirement: Concurrent consumption never overdraws
The system MUST serialize `consumeCredits` per organization (e.g.
`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) so concurrent calls cannot both pass a balance
check against the same funds.

#### Scenario: Two concurrent consumptions do not overspend
- GIVEN an org with balance 10 and a tool costing 10 credits
- WHEN two concurrent `consumeCredits` calls fire simultaneously
- THEN exactly one succeeds, the other rejects insufficient-funds, and the
  final balance is exactly 0 (never negative)

### Requirement: Cross-organization ledger isolation
A session for organization A MUST NOT read or affect organization B's
`credit_movement` rows, balance, or `subscription` via any billing API.

#### Scenario: Org A cannot read org B's ledger
- GIVEN seeded orgs A and B each with movements
- WHEN a session for org A calls any billing read/write API targeting org
  B
- THEN it returns no org B data or is denied, and org B's balance is
  unaffected

## Capability: `payment-gateway` (NEW)

### Requirement: Swappable gateway interface with idempotent apply
The system MUST define a `PaymentGateway` interface (`createTopUpIntent`,
`handleWebhookEvent`) independent of any concrete provider. Applying an
event MUST be idempotent, keyed by a `UNIQUE (gateway, externalEventId)`
constraint: re-delivery of the same event MUST be a no-op, not a second
top-up.

#### Scenario: Duplicate event applies exactly once
- GIVEN an event with `externalEventId` E already applied as a topup
- WHEN the same event E is delivered again
- THEN no second `credit_movement` is written and the balance is
  unchanged

### Requirement: Manual implementation converges on the idempotent path
V2-02's `manual` gateway (admin-triggered top-up recording with a
synthetic, admin-generated event id) MUST apply through the same
idempotent path as a future webhook implementation.

#### Scenario: Admin records a manual top-up
- GIVEN an owner/admin recording a top-up for org A
- WHEN the manual gateway generates a synthetic event id and applies it
- THEN a `topup` movement is written once, honoring the same unique
  constraint as webhook events

## Capability: `trial-credits` (NEW)

### Requirement: Verification-gated, single trial grant per email
The system MUST grant trial credits (amount from plans data, permanent —
no expiry) only after `afterEmailVerification` fires for a user, and MUST
grant at most one trial per verified email, enforced at the database
level (unique constraint), not application logic alone.

#### Scenario: First verification grants the trial
- GIVEN a user verifying their email for the first time
- WHEN `afterEmailVerification` fires
- THEN a `grant_plan`-family movement for the trial amount is written once
  for that user's org

#### Scenario: Re-verification grants no second trial
- GIVEN a user whose email was already verified and trial-granted
- WHEN their email is verified again (e.g., re-triggered flow)
- THEN the database constraint prevents a second grant and none is written

#### Scenario: Grant failure never fails verification
- GIVEN the trial-grant step throws (e.g., transient DB error)
- WHEN `afterEmailVerification` runs
- THEN the verification request still succeeds; the failure is reported
  (e.g., to Sentry), never rethrown to the caller

## Capability: `auth-foundation` (MODIFIED)

### Requirement: Email verification hook surface wired but not enforced
The system MUST wire better-auth's email verification hook surface (the
mechanism/callback path MUST exist and be invokable) but MUST NOT enforce
verification as a precondition for any flow. As of V2-02,
`afterEmailVerification` additionally dispatches
`grantTrialCreditsIfEligible` (billing module), following the never-rethrow
after-hook pattern; this dispatch MUST NOT block or fail session/
verification flows.
(Previously: hook surface wired but had no consumer; deferred enforcement
mentioned V2-01/V2-02 without naming a concrete effect.)

#### Scenario: Verification hook is invokable but not gating
- Given the auth configuration
- When a registration triggers the verification-email hook
- Then the hook surface executes without blocking session establishment
- And no endpoint rejects requests solely due to an unverified email

#### Scenario: Verification now dispatches trial-credit grant
- Given a user completes email verification
- When `afterEmailVerification` fires
- Then `grantTrialCreditsIfEligible` is invoked as a non-blocking
  after-effect (see `trial-credits` capability for grant semantics)

observations.title: sdd/v2-02-billing/design
observations.content:
Design delta (v2-02-billing) — Judgment Day Round 2 (final). Three confirmed corrections layered on round-1:

G1 idempotency: FRESH idempotency key is generated PER USER SUBMISSION (not per mount, not rotated on settled state). Rationale: recordManualTopUpAction redirects on success (NEXT_REDIRECT) so useActionState never returns a cleared state — any rotate-on-settled scheme is dead code. Pattern: pure applyFreshIdempotencyKey(formData, generateKey?) injected by a wrapped form action; double-submit protection stays with React 19 synchronous isPending disable guard.

G2 FK semantics: credit_movement.payment_event_id → payment_event(id) uses onDelete NO ACTION, NOT restrict. Rationale: both credit_movement and payment_event cascade-delete from organization; RESTRICT is immediate/non-deferrable and can block delete-organization, whereas NO ACTION defers the RI check to end-of-statement so the sibling cascade completes. Direct payment_event delete that would orphan a movement still errors. Migration 0008. Column stays nullable; partial unique index (one movement per event) unchanged.

G3 activatePlan atomicity: plan existence/isActive validation and the subscription upsert run in ONE scope.db.transaction (no TOCTOU). Throws InvalidPlanError for missing/inactive; a concurrently-deleted plan no longer surfaces as a raw FK error.

All prior design decisions (D1-D10, round-1 F1-F7) unchanged.

observations.title: V2-02 slice-3 review ESCALATED: confirmed BLOCKER — global tool_cost writable by any org owner + negative-cost credit minting
observations.content:
**What**: Slice-3 4R review (lineage review-29a180e7a43508f9, tip 5d14f2f) finalized to terminal state ESCALATED due to a CONFIRMED BLOCKER on the money path. Orchestrator independently verified against source (not just trusting the lens).

**The BLOCKER (risk lens, deterministic, introduced)**:
1. `tool_cost` is a GLOBAL table (src/shared/db/schema/billing.ts:175 — columns tool, planId, costCredits; NO organizationId). It is the platform-wide catalog.
2. `setToolCost` (src/modules/billing/plans.ts:69) gates writes only with `assertElevatedActor(actor)` = owner/admin of the actor's OWN org. Since ensureOwnerOrganization makes every self-registered user the owner of their own org, ANY registered user can overwrite the platform-global tool cost for ALL orgs.
3. `costCredits` has NO sign validation (unlike top-up amounts, which got InvalidAmountError in Phase 0). consume-credits.ts:43-52: `if (balance < cost) throw; ... amount: -cost`. A negative cost passes the guard (balance>=0 not < negative) and `-(-n)=+n` writes a POSITIVE ledger credit → any org mints unlimited credits by invoking a tool after setting its cost negative.

**Other slice-3 findings (non-blocking, to fix in the correction)**:
- [resilience+reliability WARNING] server actions (billing/actions.ts, tool-costs/actions.ts) have no try/catch around activatePlan/recordManualTopUp/setToolCost — NotAuthorizedError/InvalidAmountError propagate as opaque Next.js errors (first UI-reachable site).
- [resilience WARNING] fire-and-forget trial grant opens a test-proven eventual-consistency window (bounded: persistent node process, .catch(reportError) safe).
- [readability WARNING] resolveActor duplicated verbatim in tool-costs/actions.ts without the D7 doc comment.

**Root design gap**: design.md D1 documents tool_cost as a global catalog but never defined WHO may write a platform-global table; D7's trust boundary only reasoned about org-scoped writes. The org-facing tool-cost editor UI shipped in slice-3 exposes platform data to customer org owners — almost certainly wrong for a SaaS where tool cost reflects the platform's upstream API cost. Needs owner decision: platform-admin-only (recommended, remove org UI) vs some super-admin gate.

**Status**: Auto-chain STOPPED at owner decision. Escalated lineage is terminal — the corrected tree will need a fresh review/start. Sign validation on costCredits is unambiguous and ships regardless of the access-model decision.

**Where**: win_comerce_v1 branch v2-02/slice-3 (5d14f2f). [[decision/v2-02-product-round-v1-style-plans-seed-permanent-trial-role-only-ui-tool-cost-per-plan]]

observations.title: V2-02 slice-3 final review ESCALATED again: my own D9.2b idempotency fix introduced a cross-tenant collision (CRITICAL)
observations.content:
**What**: The final slice-3 4R review (lineage review-e12065a913d0498a, tip 8adb35c) ESCALATED on a CRITICAL that the D9.2b fix (commit 966ecf9) itself introduced. Two lenses flagged the same code: risk WARNING (assumed random-UUID key → inferential), readability CRITICAL (correctly noted the SERVER accepts arbitrary keys → deterministic). Orchestrator verified against source and accepted CRITICAL.

**The introduced CRITICAL**: D9.2b added a client-supplied idempotencyKey to manual top-ups to stop double-submit double-credit. But:
- actions.ts accepts idempotencyKey from formData with ONLY a non-empty check (form generates a UUID but server does not enforce it → attacker can POST 'a').
- manual-gateway.ts builds externalEventId = `manual:{key}` — namespaced by GATEWAY ONLY, not orgId.
- payment_event unique is UNIQUE(gateway, externalEventId) — global, no organizationId column.
- → two orgs with the same key collide globally; the loser hits applyTopUpEvent's UNIQUE-violation no-op ({applied:false}), and manual-gateway returns success WITHOUT checking applied → victim org's real top-up silently dropped while UI shows success. Cross-tenant griefing / silent credit loss.

**Lesson (important)**: when adding client-influenced idempotency keys to a multi-tenant money path, the dedup key MUST be org-namespaced. A global UNIQUE(gateway, externalEventId) was safe ONLY while ids were server-generated; making the id partly user-input silently broke that invariant. The design D9.2 even CLAIMED "never cross-tenant" while the code did not enforce it — a doc/impl mismatch a reviewer caught.

**Fix in progress (commit pending)**: (1) externalEventId = `manual:{orgId}:{key}` — collision only within same org (= genuine double-submit); (2) validate key format (bounded length + charset) instead of accepting arbitrary strings; (3) cross-org integration test: two orgs, same key → both succeed, one movement each; (4) correct design D9.2b claim.

**Where**: win_comerce_v1 v2-02/slice-3. Two escalated lineages now terminal (review-29a180e7a43508f9 the tool_cost BLOCKER, review-e12065a913d0498a this one). After fix → yet another fresh 4R review, then verify → judgment-day → archive. [[decision/v2-02-slice-3-corrected-approved-blocker-closed-platform-admin-gate-lineage-review-da5f9f83cc7ea237-]]

observations.title: V2-02 judgment-day ledger: 2 blind judges, A1 comma-role CRITICAL + B1 idempotency-key silent-drop + activatePlan validation, all verified real
observations.content:
**What**: Judgment Day on the complete v2-02-billing change (target sha256:e089deef..., lineage jd-v202-billing-35e99a5, 70 files/7832 lines). Two blind judges (A=fable, B=opus). No severe finding confirmed by BOTH, but orchestrator independently VERIFIED the impactful single-judge ones against source. Merged ledger:

**Judge A (fable)**:
- A1 CRITICAL (VERIFIED REAL): assertElevatedActor (authorization.ts:33) uses exact-match ELEVATED_ROLES.has(row.role), but better-auth stores comma-joined roles ("admin,member") — the exact bug v2-01 JD Fix 4a fixed in identity/role-utils.ts (which splits on comma, verified against org-plugin crud-members.mjs role.split(",")). Billing's page UX gate uses comma-aware isElevatedRole; billing's authoritative gate uses exact match → a legit admin with a compound role passes the UX gate but is DENIED by billing (getBillingOverview throws NotAuthorizedError in the Server Component → billing settings page errors). Fails CLOSED (availability bug, not a breach). Fix: comma-aware role check duplicated in billing (cycle-guard forbids importing identity's helper).
- A2 WARNING: trial-grant.ts eq(member.role,"owner") same comma-join miss (mainline writes "owner" exactly, so edge-case).
- A3 WARNING (OWNER DECISION): with REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=true (supported, default false), no session/owner-org exists at afterEmailVerification time → grantTrialCreditsIfEligible finds no owner membership → NO self-registered user ever gets trial, no re-trigger. Design D5 only documented this for invited-only users.
- A4 WARNING (also B2): activatePlan doesn't validate planId exists/isActive — a retired plan id can be replayed; nonexistent id → raw FK 23503 → generic error.
- A5/A6/A7 SUGGESTIONs: no FK on credit_movement.payment_event_id; updatedAt not refreshed in onConflictDoUpdate set clauses (setToolCost, activatePlan) + base-cost upsert path untested vs real PG; eslint cycle-guard pattern matches only one path segment.

**Judge B (opus)**:
- B1 WARNING (VERIFIED REAL): manual-topup-form idempotencyKey generated once per mount (useState lazy init, never regenerated); action redirects to SAME route (soft nav preserves the client component instance) → a SECOND genuinely-distinct top-up reuses the same externalEventId → applyTopUpEvent no-op → second top-up's credits SILENTLY DROPPED while UI reports success. Money-path. Fix: regenerate the key after each successful submission.
- B2 SUGGESTION = A4. B3 SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget trial grant may never settle under serverless freeze (accepted — current deploy is persistent process; owner accepted eventual consistency).

**Fix plan (round 1, per owner fix-everything policy)**: A1+A2 comma-aware role checks; B1 key regeneration; A4/B2 planId validation; A5 FK migration; A6 updatedAt refresh + base-cost test; A7 eslint pattern. A3 = owner decision (fix robustly vs document as non-default-config limitation).

observations.title: V2-02 JD re-judgment-1: both judges confirm fix-caused B1-still-broken + FK-diamond; final fix round-2 launched
observations.content:
**What**: JD scoped re-judgment (round 1) of the fix commit d55073e. Both blind judges (A=fable, B=opus) CONFIRMED A1-A7 resolved BUT found 2 fix-caused defects confirmed by BOTH:

1. **B1 STILL BROKEN (both, WARNING)**: manual-topup-key.ts `shouldRegenerateIdempotencyKey` = `wasPending && !isPending && error===null`. But recordManualTopUpAction REDIRECTS on success (throws NEXT_REDIRECT) → useActionState never returns a cleared {error:null} state on success → the key NEVER rotates on the success path. Worse, a prior failed submit leaves error sticky non-null (BillingActionState.error), so after fail→correct→success the guard stays false. Common fail→correct→success→success flow: the 2nd distinct top-up reuses the key → applyTopUpEvent no-ops on UNIQUE(gateway,externalEventId) → credits silently dropped, UI reports success. The round-1 B1 fix is ineffective.
2. **FK diamond (both — A SUGGESTION, B WARNING)**: F5's credit_movement.payment_event_id FK onDelete:restrict + both payment_event & credit_movement cascade-delete from organization = cascade diamond. RESTRICT is immediate (non-deferrable) so deleting an org with linked top-ups may raise "key still referenced" and block org/account deletion (organization plugin exposes delete-organization). New path (paymentEventId had no FK before).

Plus 1 single-judge (A) SUGGESTION: F4 activatePlan plan-validation is non-transactional check-then-write (TOCTOU) — tiny window.

**Round-2 fix plan (final round; both-confirmed + low-risk TOCTOU)**:
- B1 proper fix: generate a FRESH idempotencyKey per user-initiated submission (not per-mount, not on settled-state), relying on the disable-on-pending guard to block double-click of the SAME operation (React 19 useActionState sets isPending synchronously → 2nd click can't fire). This gives distinct top-ups distinct keys and prevents double-credit of one top-up. Test the fail→success→success flow.
- FK fix: change onDelete from `restrict` to `NO ACTION` (Postgres default, statement-level deferred check) so the org cascade completes while still preventing direct payment_event deletion that leaves a dangling movement. New migration 0008. Test org deletion with linked top-ups succeeds.
- TOCTOU: fold the plan existence/isActive lookup into the same withOrg transaction as the subscription upsert.

**Protocol state**: this is the LAST fix round (2 max). After it → re-judgment 2 (final). If still issues → escalate to owner.
**Where**: win_comerce_v1 v2-02/slice-3, JD lineage jd-v202-billing-35e99a5 open. [[decision/v2-02-judgment-day-ledger-2-blind-judges-a1-comma-role-critical-b1-idempotency-key-silent-drop-activ]]
