observations.title: Authoritative finance model: ACADEMY ECOM Excel (LEADS + MENSAJES channels)
observations.content:
**What**: The owner-provided ground-truth financial model for the Motor Financiero (more authoritative than the M3 transcriptions). File: `/home/rodrigo/Documentos/trabajos/ecomerce/Copia de ANALISIS FINANCIEROS- ACADEMY ECOM (1).xlsx` (4 sheets). Parse dump script: `/home/rodrigo/.claude/jobs/851c5fd4/tmp/dump_xlsx.py` (openpyxl).

**Sheets**: Hoja1 (primer precio), ESTABLECIENDO PRECIOS (pricing: precioMin=costoUnit/(1−margen)), ANALISIS FINANCIERO - LEADS (landing channel, full funnel P&G), ANALISIS FINANCIERO - MENSAJES (messaging channel).

**Key real formulas (LEADS)**: ventas=visualizaciones*convRate; cpaFacebook=inversion/ventas; pedidosEnviados=ventas*%confirmacion; entregasEfectivas=pedidosEnviados−ROUNDUP(%rechazo*pedidosEnviados); **cpaReal=inversion/entregasEfectivas** (≡ cpaDigital/(conf*(1−rechazo)) — MATCHES our engine). Cost structure GRANULAR: costosEnvio=pedidosEnviados*flete; costosDevoluciones=devoluciones*flete; fulfillment=entregasEfectivas*C7. profitBruto=ingresosReales−totalCostos−inversion; profitNeto=profitBruto−gastosFijos. ROAS family (3): roasFacebook=(ventas*precio)/inv, roasReal=ingresosTotales/inv, **roiAds=profitNeto/adSpend** (the "Roinads", target 100%). cpaMaxFacebook=(profitNeto+inv)/ventas; cpaMaxReal=(profitNeto+inv)/entregas; capitalMinimo=(costosPrincipal+oferta+envio+inv)/2 (LEADS biweekly) or /4 (MENSAJES weekly).

**MENSAJES channel differs**: NO confirmation stage — ventas=cantidadMensajes*cierrePorMensajes (cantidadMensajes=inversion/costoPorMensaje); pedidosEnviados=ventas; then only %rechazo attrition; cpaReal=inversion/entregas.

**Why**: Owner shared it 2026-07-23 to make the Motor Financiero reproduce the REAL model exactly. Reconciliation audit (engine vs Excel) launched.

**Learned**: Core CPA chain in our engine already matches the Excel numerically (15.84→26.4→33.06). Divergences to reconcile: granular cost structure (flete on shipped+returns, fulfillment on delivered), the full ROAS family + exact naming, cpaMax/roasMin/capitalMinimo formulas. See [[sdd/v2-05-motor-financiero/design-decisions]] and [[sdd/v2-05-motor-financiero/judgment-day]].

observations.content:
**What**: Motor Financiero (finance-engine) rebuilt from scratch to match owner's authoritative ACADEMY ECOM Excel workbook exactly. Initial model (commits 8977961..54376b2) violated core methodology (CPA breakeven as ceiling not 1.5x factor, backwards derivation vs forward-funnel projection, no fixed-cost lump). **Why**: Audit on 2026-07-23 discovered transcription-derived model did not reproduce Excel workbook's numbers. Owner approved complete rebuild with Excel as ground truth. Covers design decisions (forward-funnel, full-lump gastos fijos, 6-site Excel rounding), architecture (11 decisions R1–R11), parametrization ({canal, plataforma}), location fees, staged costs (flete on enviados+devoluciones), revenue blends (ventasTiendaWeb ventas-weighted not price-weighted), P&L (no per-order proration), ratios (distinct ROAS family), ceilings (null for unviable).

**Where**: Implementation: `src/shared/finance/` (14 files: rounding.ts, funnel.ts, revenue.ts, pnl.ts, ratios.ts, ceilings.ts, types.ts rewrite, validate.ts rewrite, cpa.ts rewrite, costs.ts rewrite, mensajes.ts rewrite, engine.ts rewrite, location-fee.ts unchanged, errors.ts unchanged; all with colocated tests; breakeven.ts/roas.ts/margins.ts deleted). observations.title: CRITICAL: Motor Financiero does NOT reproduce the real Excel — structural rework needed
observations.content:
**What**: Opus audit of the implemented Motor Financiero vs the authoritative Excel ([[finance/authoritative-excel-model]]) found the engine reproduces the CPA-ladder SHAPE and roiAds ratio but NOT the Excel's numbers. Structural defect — NOT a patch.

**Root cause**: engine uses ONE `pedidos` count read two mutually-exclusive ways — as GROSS ventas in the CPA chain (cpa.ts:47-48; engine.test.ts:18 asserts cpaDigital=spend/pedidos) and as DELIVERED entregas for ticket/costs (costs.ts:13 ticketMedio=facturacion/pedidos). Excel tracks THREE counts: ventas J15 → enviados J18=ventas·conf → entregas J22=enviados·(1−rechazo), with costs staged per funnel stage.

**Critical fixes (C1-C5)**: C1 split counts (ventas/enviados/entregas/devoluciones); reverse CPA chain to forward direction. C2 ticketMedio denominator = entregas not raw pedidos. C3 stage costs: COGS+fulfillment on ENTREGAS, flete on ENVIADOS+DEVOLUCIONES (return leg N13 currently MISSING → flete understated (1+r)/(1−r)≈1.5× at r=0.2), comision on revenue. C4 mensajes_* must NOT have a confirmation stage (ventas=enviados=J8=mensajes·cierre); validate.ts:74-84 wrongly requires pctConfirmacion for mensajes_cod. C5 ceilings = cpaMaxFacebook N28=(profitNeto+spend)/ventas, cpaMaxReal N30=(profitNeto+spend)/entregas.

**Missing metrics (M1-M7)**: roasReal=facturacion/spend, roasFacebook=(ventas·precio)/spend, capitalMinimo=(cogs+upsellCogs+fleteEnviados+spend)/divisor (2 leads/4 mensajes), profitBruto (pre-fixed), pricing-sheet markup precioMin=costoUnit/(1−margen) (likely separate module).

**Owner decisions pending (asked 2026-07-23)**: (Q1) rebuild to reproduce Excel exactly vs patch-only; (Q2) fixed costs = full monthly lump per analysis window (Excel N20) vs prorated per order (current); (Q3) rounding = Excel ROUNDUP/DOWN/ROUND on counts vs continuous (current design D9 said no-rounding — conflicts with Excel).

**Learned**: judgment-day passed because judges reviewed vs the M3-derived spec, not the Excel. The Excel is the real ground truth. The v2-05 change is NOT git-committed for archive (uncommitted working tree), so it can be revised in place. Do NOT commit the archive until the engine matches the Excel.

observations.title: Kg estimados se sumaban por embarcación en vez de por llegada
observations.content:
**What**: `estimated_quantity` vive en `acopio_arrivals` (UNA por llegada) pero las queries de KPI la sumaban sobre `acopio_arrival_assets`, multiplicándola por la cantidad de embarcaciones de la cámara. Fix: agrupar por `ar.id` con `MAX(ar.estimated_quantity)`.
**Why**: Una cámara de 1.000 kg con 3 embarcaciones reportaba 3.000 kg programados en el dashboard de acopio y en el resumen de gerencia.
**Where**: backend/src/modules/areas/areas.service.ts (getAcopioKpis — ahora GROUP BY ar.id + banderas all_programado/any_en_planta), backend/src/modules/gerencia/services/gerencia-home.service.ts (CTE por_llegada).
**Learned**: Regla de oro del modelo de acopio: lo ESTIMADO es por llegada (arrival), lo DESCARGADO es por embarcación (arrival_asset). Cualquier agregación que mezcle ambos niveles sin agrupar primero por llegada duplica. La tabla de llegadas del dashboard SÍ repite el estimado por fila a propósito (confirmado por el usuario) — solo los KPIs agregados debían cambiar. Bonus: el LATERAL de pesajes de gerencia tenía `LIMIT 1`, así que una embarcación con 2+ pesadas solo aportaba la primera.

observations.title: El pesaje de cámara va en el ANCLA, no en las embarcaciones
observations.content:
**What**: CORRIGE la memoria anterior sobre "estado del ancla derivado". Ese fix fue REVERTIDO (ac0e21c → f937100) porque el modelo era falso y rompió producción 23 min.
**Why**: Contra la BD real: `VESSEL` tiene 0 pesajes en toda la historia; `CAMARA_ANCHOR` tiene 6 y `DIRECT` 2212. El pesaje de una cámara se registra contra el ANCLA (un camión, un pesaje). Las embarcaciones de cámara son unidades DOCUMENTALES y se quedan en DOC_OK para siempre. Por eso "ancla = mínimo de sus embarcaciones" clavaba toda cámara en DOC_OK, y la migración 041 lo re-rompía en cada arranque.
**Where**: backend/src/modules/acopio/services/acopio-weighing.service.ts, areas.service.ts (CAMARA_ANCHOR_FILTER).

(2) `acopio_arrival_assets` NO tiene trigger de auditoría (data_audit_log vacío para esa tabla): los cambios de estado no dejan rastro, así que un UPDATE masivo mal hecho NO se puede revertir. observations.title: sdd/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: v2-05b-investigacion-mercado (Market Research module, M2)

### 1. Methodology ground truth (M2-L1..L6, transcripciones_limpias)

- L1 "Producto ganador": 3 conditions (demanda comprobable, economía saludable, ejecución viable) + 5 pillars: (a) dolor validado (urgente vs aspiracional), (b) márgenes saludables — targets: CPA objetivo 25-30% AOV, margen mínimo 25%, confirmación combinada Lima+provincias >50%, logística <18% AOV, costo producto <35% AOV, entrega 75-88%, ROAS>100% to scale; (c) variabilidad creativa (múltiples ángulos, no solo "wow"); (d) escalabilidad (variantes, packs/upsells, recompra, restock <=10 días); (e) viabilidad logística (<1.5kg, empaque profesional). 8-item universal checklist (soluciona dolor cotidiano, resultados visuales, validación social, fácil de explicar, precio razonable, compatible políticas ads, adaptable UGC, alta recompra, entrega simple). Explicit anti-patterns to avoid (electrónicos, tallas múltiples, receta médica, temporada).
- L2 "Cómo buscar": core method = Meta Ad Library + TikTok, NOT paid apps. ChatGPT prompt generates "palabras de dolor sin conectores" per nicho. Search ad library by pain-word, filter ads >=15 days old (durability = profitability signal = "producto quemado" = validates demand, does NOT mean avoid). Detect saturation via multiple sellers / 2x1-3x1 "oferta de salida". Core concept "cambio de vehículo": same validated pain, different product form. Cross-market check: search reference countries (CO/MX/AR/CL/US) first, then local market. TikTok used only as a SECONDARY/weaker validation signal (content-volume/virality proxy, explicitly "prueba y error", not longevity-based like Meta).
- L3 "Análisis y competencia": search both by product name AND by pain-word. Advertiser-count gate: 1-2 = good entry ("puedes meterte"), 3 = evaluate offer aggressiveness, 4+ = skip ("ni lo pienses"). Burnt signals: sold via landing AND via WhatsApp/messages simultaneously = quemado; 2x1/3x1 "oferta de salida" = dead margin. Price tiers: "precio full" (89/99/119 range) = still enterable; heavy discount tiers = saturated. Avoid MLM/pyramid products (no margin). When burnt but demand proven -> vehicle change or rebrand (not abandon). Creative reuse raises CPM — don't reuse a used creative unless new concept. TikTok validation via content/engagement volume, explicitly weaker/non-authoritative than Meta longevity.
- L4 "Proveedores": manual/human sourcing process (contact lists, import vs local vs maquila capital thresholds, mold/pote standardization warnings, quality-tier negotiation). Almost entirely a human/reference-data concern, NOT an automatable pipeline step.
- L5 "Primer costeo": manual Excel-driven pricing calculator. Target margin >=35% on single-unit sale; costoPorCompra ~=30-35% of sale price; fulfillment ~4 soles/$1 flat; anchor sale price to competitor market price (profit comes from offers/upsells, never underpricing the unit). This is literally what finance-engine's pricing/margin functions already do — must NOT be reimplemented; human enters COGS, engine computes.
- L6 "Plantilla de auditoría": final artifact is a QUALITATIVE, human/coach-reviewed audit — 10 sheets (one per candidate product), each with: product name, top-2 competitor ad links (human-picked), 2-3 observed angles, provider price + cotización link, competencia analysis (vendiendo_en_mercado, puedo_competir_en_precio, creativo_no_usado_en_mercado, creativo_ya_usado_por_mi — all boolean/manual), the 8-item L1 checklist (yes/no), free-text notes. Explicitly NO numeric score: the coach approves/rejects/asks-for-more, expects multiple rejections ("posiblemente tu coach te rechace dos, tres listas").

### 2. v1 reality (win-comerce/functions/api/agents/{producto,avatar,competencia}/run.ts + producto/approve.ts)

- **producto/run.ts** (Agent 1, 2-step): Step 1 (no dolor_elegido) = 2 parallel Brave searches + 1 LLM call generating 15 ranked "dolores" (playbook JR Consulting prompt). Step 2 (dolor_elegido given) = Apify runActorsParallel across 7 sources (Meta: pais local + CO/MX/AR/CL/US, + TikTok US), tags each ad `_pais_origen`, writes `ads_raw` to R2 (consumed later by competencia), then 4 sequential LLM calls: (1) evidencia_mercado/top_formatos/angulos, (2) market map local (nivel_saturacion, players_locales, precio_promedio_local), (3) market map exterior (oportunidades_importar, tendencias_emergentes), (4) GAP analysis producing `producto_recomendado`, `angulo_problema`, `gap_oportunidad`, **`win_rate` (0-100 scored formula: margen>60%=+25, dolor claro=+20, baja saturación=+20, wow=+15, replicable=+10, tendencia=+10)**, **`veredicto` GO/TEST/NO-GO (>=70/45-69/<45)**, and **LLM-guessed `cogs_estimado`/`precio_estimado`/`margen_estimado_pct`**. Creates a `product_approval` checkpoint (human-in-the-loop pipeline pattern already exists and is fine to reuse).
- **producto/approve.ts**: resolves the checkpoint, writes `onboarding.json` (OnboardingCC) to R2 — this becomes the shared Command-Center contract consumed by agents 2-4. **Contains dead mock-payload fallback** (`checkpoint_id.startsWith('chk_prod') || checkpoint_id === 'chk_mock'` returns a hardcoded fixture) — test scaffolding leaking into the prod code path.
- **avatar/run.ts** (Agent 2): re-runs the SAME 7-source Apify scan (dolor+producto keywords) independently of Agent 1's cached `ads_raw` (duplicate scraping cost). 4 sequential LLM calls: (1) copy_patterns per ad (angulo/pain_language/promesa/cta), (2) clustering by tema/frecuencia, (3) **Schwartz nivel_consciencia + sofisticación de mercado (1-5)** — this is M3 content, confirmed bridge, (4) avatar synthesis (avatar_principal with nombre_ficticio/demografia/jtbd/punto_a/punto_b/mensaje_clave + 2 variantes). Has a validation gate requiring punto_a/punto_b/sofisticacion_mercado non-empty (contract with downstream Copywriting agent).
- **competencia/run.ts** (Agent 3): reads Agent 1's cached `ads_raw` + `onboarding` from R2 (no re-scraping, good). Splits ads local vs referencia by tag, top-10 each by days-active. 4 LLM calls: (1) full ad deconstruction (hook_exacto, angulo, estructura, oferta, formato, physicalPosition, persuasiveLogic — genuinely M4/advertising-domain work), (2) Firecrawl landing-page CRO analysis (headline/oferta/precio/cta/trust_signals/tipo_checkout), (3) replicabilidad scoring 1-5, (4) synthesis producing angulo_dominante/**angulo_libre** (the one genuine M2 "can I enter" signal) + compliance_flags + **swipe_file** (top-8 ad references, again M4 creative-asset territory).
- `tendencia_2026` hardcode is NOT present in producto/avatar/competencia — it lives in `creativos/run.ts` (M4/Creación de Anuncios domain), out of this module's scope; owner should verify it there instead.
- Rate-limit `msg.includes('429')`-style catch-block boilerplate is duplicated per agent file (and even duplicated twice within the same catch block in producto/run.ts) — confirmed accidental complexity.

### 3. The gap (confirmed against transcriptions)

MISSING vs methodology:
- No explicit advertiser-count gate (1-2/3/4+ thresholds from L3) enforced or even surfaced as a first-class field — only an LLM-eyeballed `nivel_saturacion` enum.
- No explicit "oferta de salida" (2x1/3x1) detection as a structured signal despite already scraping ad copy/landing price.
- No cross-canal-presence-as-burnt-signal (L3: sold via landing AND via messages simultaneously = quemado) — v1 doesn't cross-reference channel presence at all.
- No L6 qualitative audit artifact (candidate batch, coach-reviewed checklist, narrative notes, explicit reject-expected workflow) — v1 jumps straight to an automated numeric verdict instead.
- No "creativo ya usado por mí" self-check (requires either a creative registry — new capability — or a manual checkbox).

INVENTED / accidental complexity (confirmed against transcriptions as DROP candidates):
- `win_rate` (0-100) + GO/TEST/NO-GO verdict: NOT in the methodology. L6 is explicitly qualitative/coach-judged with expected repeated rejection. CONFIRMED DROP.
- LLM-estimated `cogs_estimado`/`precio_estimado`/`margen_estimado_pct`: L5 teaches a human-entered-COGS Excel calculator, not an LLM guess. CONFIRMED DROP — replace with a call into `finance-engine` fed by human-entered COGS.
- Mock payload fallback in `producto/approve.ts` (`chk_mock`/`chk_prod*`): dead test scaffolding in the prod path. CONFIRMED DROP.
- Duplicated rate-limit catch-block boilerplate across agents: CONFIRMED DROP, superseded by shared-clients' own retry/fallback (already spec'd) plus job-queue's uniform step-failure handling.
- `tendencia_2026`: NOT found in producto/avatar/competencia; lives in `creativos/run.ts` (out of scope here) — flag for whichever change covers Creación de Anuncios.

### 4. Proposed module boundary (Investigación de Mercado, M2)

**OWNS** (stays in this module):
- Pain/dolor discovery (Brave + LLM), one step.
- Product-vehicle GAP analysis producing a *candidate* (not a scored verdict): producto_recomendado, angulo_problema, gap_oportunidad — no win_rate/veredicto/cogs/precio/margen.
- Local market saturation check MERGING producto's `marketLocal` + competencia's local-ads filtering into one "can I enter" concern: anunciantes_activos_count, nivel_saturacion (rule-derived from L3 thresholds, not purely LLM-eyeballed), oferta_quemada boolean, cross-canal-burnt boolean, precio_tier.
- Reference-market GAP scan (CO/MX/AR/CL/US + TikTok-as-secondary-signal).
- L6 qualitative audit artifact (checklist + narrative + human veredicto_coach) replacing the numeric win_rate.
- Human approval checkpoint (reuse existing pipeline-checkpoint pattern, drop the mock fallback).
- Pricing validation via `finance-engine` call (human-entered COGS + market-anchored price -> margenBruto/margenNeto/cpaMaxReal/etc), not LLM-estimated math.

**HANDS OFF** (per prior audit findings #1/#2, confirmed by this M2/M3/M4 read):
- To **Estrategia y Oferta (M3)**: full avatar-persona construction (nombre_ficticio, demografia, jtbd, punto_a/punto_b, Schwartz nivel_consciencia, sofisticación de mercado 1-5, mensaje_clave, variantes) — this module instead hands off a lighter `VoiceOfMarketCorpus` (raw survived-ad copy + pain-language frequency) as Estrategia y Oferta's input, not a finished avatar.
- To **Creación de Anuncios (M4)**: the deep ad deconstruction (hook_exacto, estructura, formato, physicalPosition, persuasiveLogic), landing CRO analysis, replicabilidad scoring, and swipe_file. This module keeps only a `CompetitiveLandscapeLite` (top 2-3 competitor reference URLs + observed angle, per L6's "escoge tus 2 mejores competidores") — enough to feed the human audit checkpoint, not a full creative-intelligence artifact.
- `tendencia_2026` and related creative-trend hardcodes belong to whichever change covers `creativos/run.ts` (Creación de Anuncios), not this module.

### 5. Proposed shapes (draft — not final, needs sdd-propose/sdd-spec)

```
ProductResearchContext: { projectId, pais, nicho, canal: { surface: 'landing'|'whatsapp', pago: 'gateway'|'cod' }, plataforma: 'meta'|'tiktok' }

PainCandidate (LLM, project DATA + LLM-generated): { dolor, descripcion, intensidad, frecuencia, fuente }

ProductCandidate (mixed — LLM proposal + human-entered + human-decided; up to N per batch per L6):
  producto_propuesto, dolor_asociado, angulo_problema        // LLM
  ad_links_top2: string[]                                     // human-picked
  precio_proveedor_estimado, link_cotizacion                  // human/manual, NOT LLM-estimated
  competencia: { vendiendo_en_mercado, puedo_competir_en_precio,
                 creativo_no_usado_en_mercado, creativo_ya_usado_por_mi }  // human/LLM-assisted booleans
  caracteristicas_checklist: { soluciona_problema_nicho, afecta_confianza, ahorra_tiempo,
                 ahorra_dinero, se_vende_en_packs, admite_upsell, resultado_inmediato,
                 no_requiere_esfuerzo, facil_importar_fabricar }          // 8-item L1 checklist, boolean
  notas_adicionales: string                                   // human free text
  veredicto_coach: 'approved'|'rejected'|'test'                // HUMAN decision, never computed
  razon_coach: string

MarketSignal (LLM-assisted, per candidate):
  local: { anunciantes_activos_count, nivel_saturacion, oferta_quemada, cross_canal_quemado, precio_tier, precio_promedio_local }
  referencia: { paises_con_senal: string[], oportunidades_importar: string[], tendencias_emergentes: string[] }
  tiktok_senal: { hay_contenido_viral: boolean, volumen_relativo: 'alto'|'medio'|'bajo'|'ninguno' }  // secondary/weaker per L2/L3

VoiceOfMarketCorpus (handoff to Estrategia y Oferta, NOT a full avatar):
  ads_sobrevivientes: [{ pageName, pais_origen, dias_activos, pain_language_verbatim, promesa, cta }]
  top_pain_language: [{ texto, frecuencia }]

CompetitiveLandscapeLite (handoff to Creación de Anuncios + feeds this module's own audit):
  top_2_3_referencias: [{ url, pais_origen, dias_activos, angulo_observado }]

PricingValidation (calls finance-engine.computeFinance, human enters cogs):
  input: { cogs, precio_candidato, canal, plataforma, pais }   // human-entered cogs, market-anchored precio
  output: FinanceOutputs (margenBruto, margenNeto, cpaMaxReal, roasMinReal, capitalMinimo, alerta, ...)
```

### 6. Dependencies on existing v2 capabilities

- **finance-engine** (`src/shared/finance/`, spec at `openspec/specs/finance-engine/spec.md`): `computeFinance(inputs): FinanceOutputs`. Its `FinanceInputs.canal: Canal = 'landing_cod'|'landing_pasarela'|'mensajes_cod'|'mensajes_pasarela'` and `plataforma: 'meta'|'tiktok'` and `pais` (location-fee) ALREADY implement exactly the two transversal dimensions the owner wants parametrized — this module should reuse those enums verbatim rather than inventing its own. This module supplies human-entered `cogs` + market-anchored `precio`; must NEVER re-derive margin/CPA/ROAS math itself (that was the triplication debt V2-05 Motor Financiero just paid off).
- **shared-clients** (`openspec/specs/shared-clients/spec.md`): `callLLM` (SECURITY_PREFIX + wrapUserData sanitization, model fallback chain), `braveSearch` (pain discovery, retries+empty-array-on-exhaustion), `runActorsParallel`/`AD_ACTORS`/`AD_FETCH_LIMIT` (Apify Meta+TikTok ad library, Postgres hash cache), `scrapePages` (Firecrawl SSRF-guarded, for the lite competitive-landscape reference), `getAgentModel(agentNumber)` per-agent model override.
- **job-queue**: `enqueueJob` with idempotency key + `runStepOnce` step-idempotency helper for each pipeline step (pain-discovery, market-scan, audit-compile); each step's side effects (Apify run, LLM call, R2/DB write) must be idempotent since execution is at-least-once.
- **module-access**: `withOrg()` gate on every module public API; per-store or org-wide grant check for the research module.
- **credit-ledger**: `consumeCredits(org, tool)` BEFORE each costed op (LLM call, Apify actor run, Brave search) — v1 has NO credit gating at all; this is new and mandatory (ROADMAP consideration #6).
- **agent-prompts convention** (V2-04): `src/shared/prompts/{producto,avatar,competencia}/v1.md` + `schema.ts` already exist as PROVISIONAL placeholders (explicit "V2-05 blocker" comment, AS-IS transliteration of v1 types). They must be REPLACED (not extended) with schemas reflecting the boundary cut above — dropping win_rate/veredicto/cogs_estimado/etc, adding the qualitative audit fields, and splitting avatar/competencia's non-M2 fields out into the downstream modules' own prompt schemas.

### 7. Two transversal dimensions — effect on this module

- **A — Canal de venta (surface × pago)**: does NOT change the core M2 research questions (burnt/saturation/GAP logic is channel-agnostic). It DOES: (1) tag the candidate with the target `canal` so `finance-engine`'s canal enum is available downstream; (2) become itself a piece of research EVIDENCE — L3 explicitly treats "sold via landing AND via messages simultaneously" as a burnt signal, so cross-channel presence detection should be a first-class field (`cross_canal_quemado`), not an afterthought.
- **B — Plataforma de ads (Meta vs TikTok)**: DOES change methodology confidence. Meta Ad Library (day-count filterable) is the PRIMARY, authoritative signal; TikTok is explicitly SECONDARY/weaker ("la única forma de saberlo es prueba y error" — L2/L3), engagement/view-count based rather than longevity-based. **Bug found in v1**: `avatar/run.ts` and `producto/run.ts` apply the same Meta day-based `adTier()` function to TikTok items pulled from `startDate`, which conflates two signal types the methodology explicitly says are NOT equivalent — the redesigned shape must keep `tiktok_senal` structurally separate and lower-confidence, never merged into the Meta Tier A/B/C bucket.

### Recommendation

Two structural approaches considered:
1. **Patch v1's 3-agent structure in place** (keep producto/avatar/competencia as 3 pipeline steps, only fix schemas) — Pros: minimal reshuffling, fast. Cons: perpetuates the M2/M3/M4 domain conflation the owner already flagged as wrong; downstream modules (Estrategia y Oferta, Creación de Anuncios) would still depend on artifacts owned by the wrong module. Effort: Low, but technically wrong per ROADMAP §7 decision.
2. **Recut into 1 module (Investigación de Mercado) + 2 handoff artifacts** (VoiceOfMarketCorpus to Estrategia y Oferta, CompetitiveLandscapeLite -> full deconstruction moves to Creación de Anuncios) as drafted above — Pros: matches the owner-approved ROADMAP §7 module table exactly, removes accidental complexity (win_rate, LLM-guessed COGS, mock payload) at the same time, single source of truth for canal/plataforma parametrization via finance-engine's existing enums. Cons: touches 3 agents' worth of logic, requires the two downstream modules' own SDD cycles to accept the handoff shapes. Effort: Medium.

**Recommended: Approach 2.** It is the only one consistent with the owner's 2026-07-23 decision already recorded in ROADMAP.md §7, and it retires 3 of the 4 confirmed accidental-complexity items (win_rate, LLM-cogs, mock payload) as a side effect of the boundary fix rather than a separate cleanup pass.

### Risks
- Avatar/CompetitiveLandscape handoff shapes are DRAFT only — Estrategia y Oferta and Creación de Anuncios don't have their own SDD cycles yet, so this module's "hands off" contract may need revision once those modules are actually designed (sequencing risk noted in ROADMAP §7 point 1, still ABIERTO).
- Dropping win_rate/veredicto changes the human checkpoint UX materially (from "approve this score" to "review this qualitative audit") — needs product/UX sign-off, not just backend.
- Open question #2 below (batch-of-N-candidates vs one-candidate-per-run) materially changes the data model and must be resolved before sdd-spec.

### Open questions for the owner
1. Confirm avatar full-persona construction (nombre_ficticio, demografia, JTBD, punto_a/b, Schwartz, sofisticación) moves entirely to Estrategia y Oferta, with this module handing off only the raw VoiceOfMarketCorpus — or does the human checkpoint UI still need a lightweight avatar draft rendered here?
2. Does V2 keep L6's "batch of up to 10 candidates reviewed together, coach expects to reject several" workflow, or move to one-candidate-per-pipeline-run (matching V2-05's `pipeline_run` single-artifact model)? This changes the data model (array vs single record).
3. Should "creativo_ya_usado_por_mi" require a new creative-registry capability, or stay a manual self-report checkbox at MVP?
4. Should the L3 advertiser-count thresholds (1-2/3/4+) be a HARD gate blocking progression, or advisory-only (surfaced number, human decides) — consistent with dropping win_rate's automated verdict?
5. Confirm L4/L5 (supplier sourcing, manual costing) stay OUT of this module's pipeline scope — supplier contact lists as reference content, costing as a finance-engine call with human-entered COGS only, no supplier-matching agent.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes, with the 5 open questions above needing owner answers before or during sdd-propose (they affect scope, not just detail).

El scraper v3.1 está activo y avanzando correctamente en segundo plano. Diagnóstico de la pausa previa: (1) El script v3 original se quedó colgado en un bucle infinito en scroll_page porque pos < document.body.scrollHeight nunca terminaba en páginas dinámicas. (2) Se corrigió scroll_page con un límite máximo de 15 pasos. (3) Se eliminó __sessid de la configuración de proxy que causaba ERR_PROXY_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED en Playwright. (4) Se implementó descubrimiento dinámico de URLs desde las páginas base de cada país. (5) Estado actual: 863 URLs de listado encoladas dinámicamente, procesando países activamente.

observations.title: V2-05b Investigación de Mercado — owner scope decisions
observations.content:
**What**: Owner resolved the 5 open scope questions from the v2-05b exploration (Engram #610), unblocking sdd-propose.

1. **Avatar moves ENTIRELY to Estrategia y Oferta (M3)**. Investigación de Mercado hands off only `VoiceOfMarketCorpus` (raw surviving-ad copy + pain-language frequency). No lightweight avatar draft rendered at the M2 checkpoint — one owner per datum.
2. **Batch of N candidates** (faithful to course L6: up to 10 candidate sheets reviewed together, repeated rejection expected). Data model is an ARRAY, not one-candidate-per-pipeline_run. Side-by-side comparison is part of the method.
3. **Advertiser-count thresholds (L3: 1-2 / 3 / 4+) are ADVISORY ONLY** — surface the number plus the course reading, human decides. Rationale: dropping win_rate's automatic verdict and then adding a hard gate would reintroduce automated judgment through the back door in a module defined as qualitative.
4. **"Creativo ya usado por mí" = manual checkbox at MVP.** No creative-registry capability in this change; it would encroach on the not-yet-designed Creación de Anuncios (M4) module.
5. **CONFIRMED (orchestrator assumption, not contradicted)**: L4 (supplier sourcing) and L5 (manual costing) stay OUT of pipeline scope — suppliers as reference content only, costing as a `finance-engine` call with human-entered COGS.

**Why**: These five affect SCOPE, not detail, and had to be resolved before the proposal phase. Questions 1, 2 and 4 each change the data model or the module boundary.

**Where**: `win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/exploration.md` §10; ROADMAP.md §7.

**Learned**: The `Canal`/`Plataforma`/`pais` unions already shipped in `src/shared/finance/types.ts` (V2-05 Motor Financiero) ARE the two transversal dimensions the owner wanted parametrized — downstream modules reuse them verbatim instead of inventing their own. Also: v1 bug confirmed — `producto/run.ts` and `avatar/run.ts` apply Meta's day-based `adTier()` to TikTok items, conflating longevity and engagement signals the course explicitly treats as non-equivalent.

observations.title: sdd/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: v2-05b — Market Research module (Investigación de Mercado, M2)

File: `win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/proposal.md` (authoritative copy, identical content).

Rebuild the pipeline entry point as one domain module that gathers evidence and lets the human judge, replacing v1's three mis-cut agents (`producto`, `avatar`, `competencia`) and their invented automation.

Proposal question round: resolved via binding owner decisions (avatar → M3; batch-of-N candidates; advisory-only thresholds; manual creative checkbox; L4/L5 out of pipeline).

## Intent
v1 conflates M2/M3/M4 domains and replaces the course's qualitative coach audit (L6) with invented judgment: `win_rate` 0-100, GO/TEST/NO-GO, LLM-guessed COGS/price/margin. Rebuild M2 so automation only structures market evidence and every verdict is human.

## Scope — In
- Research run: pain discovery (LLM + Brave), single cached 7-source Meta/TikTok ad scan, local saturation + reference-market analysis.
- Batch data model: ARRAY of ProductCandidate per run (L6 workflow).
- Advisory advertiser-count (1-2 / 3 / 4+ surfaced; no hard gate).
- Structured burnt signals: 2x1/3x1 exit-offer detection; cross-channel (landing AND messages).
- L6 qualitative audit artifact + human coach verdict checkpoint (approved|rejected|test); manual "creative already used by me" checkbox.
- Handoffs: VoiceOfMarketCorpus → Estrategia y Oferta (M3); CompetitiveLandscapeLite (top 2-3 refs) → Creación de Anuncios (M4).
- PricingValidation via computeFinance with human-entered COGS; reuse Canal/Plataforma/pais from src/shared/finance/types.ts verbatim.
- Replace provisional schemas in src/shared/prompts/{producto,avatar,competencia}/.
- Plumbing: withOrg() on all entry points, consumeCredits before every costed op, idempotent runStepOnce steps.
- Bug fix: tiktok_senal structurally separate, lower-confidence; never merged into Meta day-tier buckets.

## Scope — Out (non-goals)
Avatar persona (M3, no draft at checkpoint); ad deconstruction/CRO/swipe file + tendencia_2026 (M4); supplier automation (L4 reference content); any local margin/CPA/ROAS math; creative registry; win_rate or any automated verdict; mock-payload fallback.

## Capabilities
- NEW `market-research`: M2 pipeline, market signals, candidate batch, L6 audit checkpoint, two handoff contracts.
- MODIFIED `agent-prompts`: provisional producto/avatar/competencia schemas REPLACED; provisional-pending-V2-05 marker retires for those agents (delta spec).

## Approach
Exploration approach 2 (recut into one module + two handoff artifacts). Flow: ProductResearchContext → PainCandidate[] → cached ad scan → MarketSignal (local/referencia/tiktok_senal) → ProductCandidate[] batch → human audit checkpoint → handoffs + PricingValidation. Automation gathers; humans decide.

## Delivery shape (flagged)
Exceeds 800-line review budget → chained slices, stacked-to-main:
1. Shapes + Zod schemas + agent-prompts delta (no runtime).
2. Research-run job-queue steps: scan, signals, credit gating, idempotency.
3. Audit checkpoint + human verdict + handoffs + pricing validation.
Each slice TDD-first, autonomous, independent rollback.

## Risks
- Handoff shapes drafted before M3/M4 SDD cycles (High) → version contracts, revisit at M3/M4 propose.
- Scan/LLM cost per batched run (Med) → consumeCredits gate; reuse cached ads_raw.
- Non-idempotent side effects under at-least-once execution (Med) → idempotency keys per step, persist-once writes, tests.
- Checkpoint UX shift score→qualitative (Low) → owner-approved; UI review slice 3.

## Rollback
Additive module + new tables only: revert slice PR(s), restore provisional schemas from git, drop new tables. No tenant-data migration.

## Success criteria
Run yields candidate batch with advisory signals and NO automated verdict field; checkpoint renders L6 audit with persisted human verdict+reason; both handoff artifacts persisted; pricing only via computeFinance; tests prove withOrg + consumeCredits everywhere; test proves TikTok never enters Meta tier bucket.

observations.title: sdd/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/design
observations.content:
# Design: v2-05b — Market Research module (M2)

File: `win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/design.md` (authoritative copy, identical content).

## Technical Approach
New module `src/modules/market-research/`: Drizzle org-scoped tables (`withOrg()` only inside module public API), two job types on the existing worker (`runStepOnce` per step), all external I/O via `shared-clients`, pricing delegated to `computeFinance`. Automation gathers evidence into a candidate batch; every verdict is a human write. Three stacked slices confirmed.

## Architecture Decisions
- **D1 Batch model**: `research_run` aggregate root (status `pains_ready → scanning → awaiting_review → reviewed`) + N `product_candidate` rows each with its OWN nullable `veredicto_coach`/`razon_coach`/`reviewed_at`. Partial approval = row-level fact; run stays `awaiting_review` until all candidates have verdicts and review is closed; verdicts editable until close, frozen after. Rejected: JSON array on run (races, no per-candidate constraints); one-candidate-per-run (contradicts owner decision #612).
- **D2 Idempotency (layered)**: (a) `enqueueJob` keys `mr:pains:{runId}` / `mr:scan:{runId}`; (b) stable step keys per job (`ad-scan`, `signal-local`, `signal-tiktok`, `candidate-draft`, `corpus`, `finalize`) with ONE LLM call per step so crash re-executes at most one call; (c) all in-step DB writes use deterministic natural keys + unique index + `onConflictDoNothing`: `research_ad (run_id, source, external_id)`, `product_candidate (run_id, ordinal)`, `research_handoff (run_id, contract)`. `runStepOnce` = exactly-once RECORDING, at-least-once EXECUTION → step fns must converge.
- **D3 Single ad scan**: one `ad-scan` step normalizes 7 sources into `research_ad` rows; signal steps AND corpus read those rows (v1 avatar re-scrape structurally impossible). Cross-run reuse via existing `search_cache` apify key `sha256("apify:" + JSON({actorId,input,maxItems}))` using `AD_ACTORS`/`AD_FETCH_LIMIT` verbatim (documented cross-agent contract in apify.ts). Raw ads NOT stored in `job_step.result_json` (counts+ids only).
- **D4 Credit gating**: scan probes `cacheGet("apify", cacheInput)` per source with client-identical key BEFORE `consumeCredits`; debit only uncached sources. LLM/Brave steps debit inside their step immediately before the call. Replay of recorded step never re-debits; crash between debit and step record re-debits once — accepted at-least-once window, documented + tested. Rejected: debit-always (burns credits on cache HIT); pre-charge hook in shared-clients (scope creep).
- **D5 Handoff versioning**: `VoiceOfMarketCorpusV1`, `CompetitiveLandscapeLiteV1`; envelope `{contract, version: 1, payload}` in `research_handoff` (contract + version columns); M3/M4 add V2 additively; consumers pin via `z.discriminatedUnion("version", ...)`.
- **D6 Prompt replacement**: keep `src/shared/prompts/{producto,avatar,competencia}/` dirs; add `v2.md` + rewrite `schema.ts`+tests: producto → pipeline schemas (pain-discovery, market-signal, candidate-draft), avatar → `voiceOfMarketCorpusV1Schema`, competencia → `competitiveLandscapeLiteV1Schema`. `agent-prompts` delta retires byte-identical-v1 and provisional-marker requirements for these three only. Zod schemas stay in shared/prompts (modules import shared, never reverse — eslint-boundaries).
- **D7 TikTok type-level separation**: `AdItem = MetaAdItem | TikTokAdItem` discriminated on `platform`; only `MetaAdItem` has `startDate/diasActivos/tier`; `metaTier(ad: MetaAdItem)`; `MarketSignalV1.local.adsRef: MetaAdRef[]`. TikTok into Meta tier = compile error + zod discriminatedUnion runtime rejection. Fixes confirmed v1 bug.
- **D8 No automated verdict, structurally**: no shape/table/schema contains `win_rate`/auto-`veredicto`/`cogs_estimado`/`precio_estimado`/`margen_estimado_pct`. `lectura_advisoria` (`1-2_entrada|3_evaluar|4_mas_evitar`) is rule-derived advisory label, never a gate. Structural test asserts forbidden keys rejected by every output schema.
- **D9 Slices confirmed**: S1 shapes + Zod + prompts v2 + agent-prompts delta (no runtime/tables); S2 Drizzle schema + migration + job handlers + steps + credit gating + idempotency; S3 checkpoint API/UI + human verdict + close-review + handoff writes + PricingValidation. Each <800 lines, TDD-first, independently revertible.

## Data Flow
POST run (withOrg) → research_run → enqueue `mr:pains:{runId}` → pains job (credits→brave×2+LLM → PainCandidate[] → pains_ready) → human picks dolor → enqueue `mr:scan:{runId}` → ad-scan (probe cache→credits miss-only→runActorsParallel→research_ad) → signal-local (rules+1 LLM, Meta rows) + signal-tiktok (rules, TikTok rows) → candidate-draft (1 LLM → candidate rows) → corpus → finalize → awaiting_review. Checkpoint: human edits candidate fields, per-candidate verdict, COGS → `computeFinance` (pure, no credits) → pricing snapshot. Close review → freeze verdicts → write research_handoff (corpus + landscape) → reviewed.

## Key shapes
Reuses `Canal`/`Plataforma`/`pais` from `src/shared/finance/types.ts` verbatim. ProductCandidate = LLM draft (productoPropuesto, dolorAsociado, anguloProblema) + human fields (adLinksTop2, precioProveedor, linkCotizacion, checklist×8, competencia×4 incl. creativoYaUsadoPorMi checkbox, notas) + veredictoCoach `approved|rejected|test|null` (HUMAN write only) + razonCoach. PricingValidation = { input(human cogs, Canal, Plataforma, pais), output: FinanceOutputs } snapshot.

## Files
S1: `src/modules/market-research/{shapes,signals,tiktok,corpus}.ts`+tests; prompts v2 replacements; specs (market-research new, agent-prompts delta). S2: `src/shared/db/schema/market-research.ts` + migration `00xx_add_market_research_tables.sql` (research_run, product_candidate, research_ad, research_handoff — all org FK cascade); `{run,pains-job,scan-job,credits-gate}.ts` + registration in `src/worker/handlers.ts` jobRegistry. S3: `{checkpoint,verdict,close-review,pricing}.ts`, app routes/UI, module `index.ts` public API.

## Testing
Unit: signal rules, lectura advisoria, burnt detection, corpus, D7 compile-time type-error fixture + zod rejection, D8 forbidden-field structural test. Integration: step replay (same jobId twice → zero duplicate rows AND zero duplicate credit_movement), cache-HIT scan → zero apify debit, withOrg isolation on 4 tables, verdict frozen after close (precedent: consume-credits.race.integration.test.ts). E2E: Playwright checkpoint flow incl. partial verdicts + pricing + handoffs.

## Threat Matrix
N/A — no routing/shell/subprocess/VCS boundary; HTTP only via shared-clients; handlers run in existing worker process.

## Migration/Rollback
Additive only (4 new tables). Revert slice PRs, drop tables, restore prompt schemas from git. No tenant data migrated.

## Open
None blocking. research_handoff V1 payloads expected to be revised at M3/M4 propose (absorbed by D5).

observations.title: V2-05b design addendum D10 — batch ceiling
observations.content:
**What**: Added decision D10 to `v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/design.md` after a fresh-context phase-contract validation found the only coverage gap: the spec requires "up to 10 ProductCandidate records" per run, and the design had no mechanism for the ceiling. D10 = `MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_RUN = 10` exported from `shapes.ts`, enforced in the `candidate-draft` step and asserted by a unit test; the existing `product_candidate (run_id, ordinal)` unique index (D2) is the enforcement surface. Rejected a hard DB CHECK constraint — the cap is a product parameter that will move, not a data-integrity invariant.

**Why**: Auto-mode gatekeeper requires a fresh-context phase-contract validator for sdd-design. Verdict was PASS_WITH_NOTES with this single uncovered requirement. Amended inline rather than re-running the design phase (one-row edit).

**Where**: `win_comerce_v1/openspec/changes/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/design.md` (D10 row). The Engram design observation #615 predates this addendum — the FILE is authoritative for D10.

**Learned**: The validator verified every code symbol the design cites against the real repo — all exist. It specifically confirmed the apify cache key is exactly `sha256("apify:" + JSON({actorId,input,maxItems}))` (`src/shared/clients/{cache,apify}.ts`), which means the design's own self-flagged "cache-key drift" risk in D3/D4 is accurate, not speculative. observations.title: gentle-ai capture-result schema mismatch blocks native receipt
observations.content:
**What**: `gentle-ai review capture-result` (v2.1.11) rejects reviewer-result JSON built from the documented lens output shape. Errors: `decode reviewer result: json: unknown field "summary"` and `unknown field "classification"`. The sanctioned discovery path (`gentle-ai review capabilities --contract gentle-ai.review-integration/v1`, queried once) lists the schema id `https://gentle-ai.dev/schema/review/reviewer/v1` but does NOT expose its field list. Per the review execution contract the orchestrator must not explore commands or guess payload formats to construct authority bytes, so the native lifecycle was STOPPED at capture, not faked.

Consequence: no receipt exists for lineage `review-caddab7c0a9492da`, so `gentle-ai review validate --gate pre-commit` cannot bind, and the commit/push path is blocked pending an owner decision.

**Why**: First time in this project that the native bounded-review lifecycle was driven from Claude Code rather than OpenCode. OpenCode has a managed hook that performs capture-result automatically; Claude Code does not, so the payload must be constructed by hand — and its schema is not discoverable through the sanctioned path.

**Where**: `win_comerce_v1`, branch `v2-05b/slice-1a`. Lens outputs preserved at `<scratchpad>/lens-{risk,resilience,readability,reliability}.json`; frozen candidate diff at `<scratchpad>/candidate-A.diff`.

**Learned**: The substantive review is NOT blocked by this — a full fresh-context 4R sweep ran against the frozen candidate tree (`gentle-ai review start` succeeded: lineage `review-caddab7c0a9492da`, risk `high`, 1507 changed lines, correction budget 200). Only the receipt bookkeeping is blocked. To unblock permanently, obtain the `review/reviewer/v1` field list (schema URL, vendor docs, or an OpenCode-captured example artifact) and record it as the canonical payload template for Claude Code sessions.

## Goal
Ajustes de extracción documental de acopio, placa de cámara en el dashboard, kg estimados mal sumados, y el descuadre de kg descargados en cámaras. Todo commiteado y desplegado a producción.

## Instructions
- El usuario exige verificar contra evidencia real antes de afirmar. Se incumplió una vez (migración con modelo no verificado → rompió producción 23 min) y se corrigió el método: desde entonces, toda query se probó read-only contra la BD de producción ANTES de desplegar.
- Deploy: push a main → runners self-hosted en la VM (backend/infra). Frontend en Vercel.
- Commits en español, conventional commits, sin atribución a IA.

## Discoveries
- Las migraciones de vértebra SÍ corren solas al arrancar el backend (evidencia: document_type_catalog.updated_at coincide con el deploy, ZARPE intacto). Antes se afirmó lo contrario y era falso.
- MODELO CORRECTO de acopio: kg estimados = UNO por llegada/cámara (global, se cuenta una sola vez); kg descargados = POR EMBARCACIÓN. Mezclar niveles sin agrupar duplica.

- Migración 040: guía de remitente sin código de habilitación del muelle (no está impreso en el documento), formato de desembarque sin fecha y opcional en BARCO. Viva en producción.

observations.title: Fixed credit re-debit on pains-job retry (one costed call per step)
observations.content:
**What**: Split `runPainDiscovery` from ONE `runStepOnce("pain-discovery")` wrapping 3 non-idempotent `consumeCredits` debits into FOUR steps with stable keys: `pain-discovery-brave-general`, `pain-discovery-brave-forum`, `pain-discovery-llm`, `pain-discovery-finalize`. Added `PAINS_SIN_DATOS_STATUS = "pains_sin_datos"`: when BOTH Brave searches return `[]`, the LLM is never debited or called and the run parks in a human-visible state.
**Why**: `runStepOnce` records a step only AFTER `fn()` resolves. Any throw (LLM retry exhaustion, zod parse reject, crash) made `failJob` requeue and re-execute all three debits. `consumeCredits` has no idempotency key. Violated spec "Idempotent pipeline steps under at-least-once execution" and design D2(b).
**Where**: src/modules/market-research/pains-job.ts, pains-job.test.ts, NEW pains-job.replay.integration.test.ts, run.ts (uses shared `@/shared/jobs/generate-id` now), src/shared/db/schema/market-research.ts (status comment), openspec/changes/v2-05b-investigacion-mercado/{design,tasks,specs/market-research/spec}.md
**Learned**: A naive "invoke handler twice with same jobId" test does NOT reproduce this bug — `runStepOnce` replays cleanly on the happy path. The RED test must make attempt 1 CRASH after the Brave debits (mock `callLLM` to reject once), then assert Brave `credit_movement` rows stay at 2 not 4. Confirmed RED at 4 before the fix. `braveSearch` returns `[]` on exhausted retries rather than throwing, which is why zero evidence was silently billable. `MAX_DOLORES` was already enforced by `painDiscoverySchema`'s `.max()` — finding 4b was a false positive, covered by a new test instead of new code. Suite: 677 -> 682 passed.

Métricas actuales y reinicio del scraper en la VM GCP escorpia: (1) Total sellos descubiertos en la sesión: 10,824 sellos. (2) Páginas de listado completadas en la VM: 1,129 páginas. (3) Cobertura de imágenes HD en Cloudflare D1: 30,416 sellos con imagen (95.4% de cobertura total). (4) Sellos sin imagen restantes: 1,456 sellos. (5) Motores relanzados y activos en la VM (PIDs 3197868 y 3197869). Tasa media de extracción: ~3 sellos por segundo.

observations.title: Credit re-debit on job retry — three lenses, one blocker
observations.content:
**What**: `pains-job.ts` bundled THREE non-idempotent credit debits (Brave×2 + LLM) inside a single `runStepOnce("pain-discovery")` step. `runStepOnce` records a step only AFTER its `fn()` resolves, so any throw inside it (LLM retries exhausted, `schema.parse` on malformed JSON, insufficient credits, worker crash) records nothing → `failJob` requeues up to `JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) → the retry re-executes everything and re-bills all three calls. `consumeCredits` takes no idempotency key and inserts a fresh `credit_movement` unconditionally.

Fixed by splitting into four steps with stable keys — `pain-discovery-brave-general`, `pain-discovery-brave-forum`, `pain-discovery-llm`, `pain-discovery-finalize` — each wrapping exactly ONE costed call and returning its result so a replay reads the record.

**Why**: It contradicted the change's own design D2(b) ("one LLM call per step so a crash re-executes at most one call") and violated its own spec requirement ("Re-running a step after a crash MUST NOT incur duplicate LLM spend"). Found by 3 independent review lenses (risk, reliability, resilience) converging with concrete failure sequences — deterministic, so no refuter batch was needed.

**Where**: `win_comerce_v1/src/modules/market-research/pains-job.ts`, new `pains-job.replay.integration.test.ts`. Shipped in PR #12 (commit 8c5fae7).

**Learned — the root cause of the root cause**: the unit test stubbed `runStepOnce` as `<T>(_key, fn) => fn()`, so it ALWAYS executed and never exercised record-then-replay. A test that cannot fail is not a test. Any future job-handler test in this repo that fakes `runStepOnce` this way is blind to the entire idempotency contract — the replay path needs a REAL `runStepOnce` bound to a REAL `job` row (see `pains-job.replay.integration.test.ts`, proven RED first with "expected 4 to be 2" on Brave `credit_movement` rows).

Second fix in the same pass: `braveSearch` returns `[]` when its retries are exhausted rather than throwing, so a Brave outage silently bought an LLM call whose output was indistinguishable from a real result. Both searches empty now parks the run at `pains_sin_datos` WITHOUT debiting — same convention as `lecturaAdvisoria` returning `sin_datos` at a zero count. Consequence to handle in S3: a `pains_sin_datos` run cannot be recovered by retrying the same job (the empty Brave steps are recorded), so the UI must offer "start a new run".

One reported finding was a FALSE POSITIVE: `MAX_DOLORES` was already enforced by `painDiscoverySchema.max()`. Locked with a test instead of adding redundant runtime code.

observations.title: SDD Specification: collection-and-automatch
observations.content:
# SDD Specification: collection-and-automatch

## Capability
Capability ID: `user-collections-and-automatch`

---

## REQ-COL-001: Google OAuth & Session Authentication

### Description
Implement user authentication supporting Google OAuth 2.0 flow and credential login, session cookie management (`fp_session`), and D1 user account creation/retrieval.

### API Specification
- `POST /api/auth/login`: Authenticate with email/password credentials or session token check.
- `GET /api/auth/google`: Initiate or handle Google OAuth 2.0 redirection and callback, creating or linking D1 user record.
- `POST /api/auth/logout`: Invalidate session cookie `fp_session`.

### BDD Scenarios

#### Scenario 1: User logs in successfully via Google OAuth
- **Given** an unauthenticated user navigating to the login page
- **When** the user clicks "Iniciar sesión con Google" and authorizes access with email "collector@example.com"
- **Then** a D1 user account is created if non-existent, a secure `fp_session` cookie is issued, and the user is redirected to `/perfil`.

#### Scenario 2: Session validation on protected route
- **Given** an HTTP request to `/api/collection` with a valid `fp_session` cookie
- **When** the session middleware processes the request
- **Then** the request is authenticated and the current user's profile and ID are injected into the handler context.

#### Scenario 3: Unauthenticated access rejection
- **Given** an HTTP request to `/api/collection` without a `fp_session` cookie or with an expired session
- **When** the session middleware processes the request
- **Then** the API responds with HTTP 401 Unauthorized and JSON `{"error": "Unauthenticated"}`.

---

## REQ-COL-002: D1 UserCollection Schema Migration v6

### Description
Define and apply D1 migration v6 to create the `UserCollection` table storing stamps across three list types (`collection`, `wishlist`, `trade`) with condition grades (`MNH`, `MH`, `Used`, `FDC`).

### Schema Definition
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS UserCollection (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  stamp_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  list_type TEXT CHECK(list_type IN ('collection', 'wishlist', 'trade')) NOT NULL,
  condition TEXT CHECK(condition IN ('MNH', 'MH', 'Used', 'FDC')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MNH',
  notes TEXT,
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  UNIQUE(user_id, stamp_id, list_type)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_collection_user_type ON UserCollection(user_id, list_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_collection_stamp ON UserCollection(stamp_id);
```

### BDD Scenarios

#### Scenario 1: Adding a stamp to collection with condition grade
- **Given** an authenticated user with ID "user_123"
- **When** the user adds stamp "stamp_chile_1853_1" to their wishlist with condition "MNH" and note "Buscando buena centrada"
- **Then** a record is inserted into `UserCollection` with `list_type = 'wishlist'` and `condition = 'MNH'`, enforcing unique constraint `(user_id, stamp_id, list_type)`.

#### Scenario 2: Updating stamp condition and notes
- **Given** an existing entry in `UserCollection` for user "user_123" and stamp "stamp_chile_1853_1" in list "trade"
- **When** the user changes condition from "Used" to "MH" and updates notes
- **Then** the record `condition` and `updated_at` timestamp are updated without creating duplicate entries.

---

## REQ-COL-003: /perfil 3-Tab Inventory Dashboard & Quick Cards

### Description
Implement a 3-tab user inventory dashboard on `/perfil` (Colección, Deseos, Intercambio) with condition filters, and attach interactive quick-toggle buttons (`+ Colección`, `+ Deseos`, `+ Intercambio`) to catalog stamp cards.

### UI & Component Specs
- **Dashboard Tabs**: `/perfil` renders tabs for `Colección`, `Deseos`, and `Intercambio`.
- **Condition Filters**: Filter list items by `MNH`, `MH`, `Used`, `FDC`.
- **Quick Action Buttons**: Catalog cards feature toggle buttons to add/remove stamps from user lists instantly.

### BDD Scenarios

#### Scenario 1: Displaying user collections on /perfil dashboard
- **Given** an authenticated collector visiting `/perfil`
- **When** the user clicks on the "Intercambio" tab
- **Then** all stamps marked with `list_type = 'trade'` for this user are rendered with their condition badges and quick removal/edit controls.

#### Scenario 2: Quick toggle stamp addition from catalog card
- **Given** an authenticated user browsing catalog cards on `/catalogo`
- **When** the user clicks the `+ Deseos` button on stamp card "stamp_chile_1900_5"
- **Then** an API call is made to `POST /api/collection`, the button toggles state to active ("En Deseos"), and the stamp is added to the user's wishlist.

---

## REQ-COL-004: 2-Way Reciprocal Auto-Match Engine

### Description
Implement `/api/match` computing reciprocal trade matches between User A and User B by finding the 2-way set intersection:
1. (User A Trade ∩ User B Wishlist)
2. (User B Trade ∩ User A Wishlist)
Returns match percentage and specific trade proposals.

### Algorithm Definition
- **Set A_trade**: Stamps User A offers for trade.
- **Set A_wish**: Stamps User A desires.
- **Set B_trade**: Stamps User B offers for trade.
- **Set B_wish**: Stamps User B desires.
- **Match A -> B**: M_AB = A_trade ∩ B_wish
- **Match B -> A**: M_BA = B_trade ∩ A_wish
- **Reciprocal Match Condition**: Valid match requires |M_AB| > 0 and |M_BA| > 0.
- **Match Score**: Score = (|M_AB| + |M_BA|) / (|A_wish| + |B_wish|) * 100%

### BDD Scenarios

#### Scenario 1: Computing reciprocal trade matches between two collectors
- **Given** User A with Trade=[S1, S2, S3] and Wishlist=[S4, S5]
- **And** User B with Trade=[S4, S6] and Wishlist=[S1, S7]
- **When** `/api/match` is executed for User A
- **Then** User B is identified as a reciprocal match with M_AB = [S1] and M_BA = [S4], returning match proposals with calculated percentage.

#### Scenario 2: Excluding non-reciprocal matches
- **Given** User A with Trade=[S1] and Wishlist=[S2]
- **And** User C with Trade=[S2] and Wishlist=[S3] (has item User A wants, but wants nothing User A has)
- **When** `/api/match` is executed for User A
- **Then** User C is excluded from trade match proposals because |M_AC| = 0.

observations.title: SDD Technical Design: collection-and-automatch
observations.content:
# SDD Technical Design: collection-and-automatch

## Capability
Capability ID: `user-collections-and-automatch`

---

## Technical Approach

The `collection-and-automatch` capability delivers user collection management, Google OAuth authentication, and a reciprocal trade engine for the Filatelia platform.

1. **Authentication & Session Management**: Expand user authentication to support Google OAuth 2.0 PKCE flow (`/api/auth/google`) alongside existing credential login. Sessions are persisted in Cloudflare D1 and identified via the `fp_session` HTTP-only secure cookie.
2. **Database Schema (D1 Migration v6)**: Introduce `UserCollection` table storing stamp inventory partitioned into three lists (`collection`, `wishlist`, `trade`) with philatelic condition grades (`MNH`, `MH`, `Used`, `FDC`). Enforce unique constraints and compound indexes.
3. **RESTful Collection API**: Provide `/api/collection` supporting `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` for managing item entries, notes, and condition grades with strict session verification and input validation.
4. **Reciprocal Trade Engine**: Implement `/api/match` to calculate 2-way reciprocal trade compatibility between active collectors:
   - Matches items Collector A offers for trade against items Collector B desires (`M_AB = A_trade ∩ B_wish`).
   - Matches items Collector B offers for trade against items Collector A desires (`M_BA = B_trade ∩ A_wish`).
   - Requires reciprocal non-zero match (`|M_AB| > 0` AND `|M_BA| > 0`) and calculates match score percentage.
5. **Frontend UI Integration**: Upgrade `/perfil` to feature a 3-tab inventory dashboard (`Colección`, `Deseos`, `Intercambio`) with condition badges, and add quick-action toggle buttons (`+ Colección`, `+ Deseos`, `+ Intercambio`) to stamp cards on `/catalogo`.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision 1: Relational D1 UserCollection Table vs. Document/JSON Column

**Choice**: Dedicated relational table `UserCollection` in Cloudflare D1 with composite indexes and SQL CHECK constraints.  
**Alternatives considered**: Storing collection data as a JSON blob array in the `User` table.  
**Rationale**: 2-way reciprocal trade calculations require querying and set-intersecting items across all system users. A relational table with `idx_user_collection_user_type` enables fast targeted queries, strict ENUM validation, and pagination.

### Decision 2: Edge-Compatible Google OAuth 2.0 PKCE Flow

**Choice**: Direct Edge-compatible Google OAuth 2.0 integration via Next.js Route Handlers (`/api/auth/google`) using standard `fetch` and web crypto APIs.  
**Alternatives considered**: NextAuth.js / Auth.js library integration.  
**Rationale**: Cloudflare Workers/D1 Edge runtime has strict bundle size limits and non-Node.js standard execution environment. Direct implementation guarantees zero external runtime dependencies and seamless integration with existing `fp_session` cookie handling.

### Decision 3: Server-side Reciprocal Match Calculation Engine

**Choice**: Process reciprocal trade intersections in-memory within the `/api/match` route handler using structured set intersections.  
**Alternatives considered**: Complex SQL recursive CTE join queries on D1 or client-side evaluation.  
**Rationale**: In-memory set intersection on indexed D1 query results minimizes D1 CPU cycles while completing score calculations in linear time (`O(N + M)`), returning structured match proposals directly to the client.

---

## Data Flow

```
[ User Browser / UI ]
   │
   ├─► Google OAuth / Login ──► GET /api/auth/google ──► Google OAuth Provider / D1 User Session
   │                                  │
   │                             Set fp_session Cookie
   │                                  │
   ├─► Manage Inventory ──────► GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/collection ──► D1 UserCollection Table
   │                                  │
   ├─► Catalog Quick Action ──► POST /api/collection ────────────────► D1 UserCollection Table
   │                                  │
   └─► Auto-Match Search ─────► GET /api/match ────────────────────────► Trade Intersect Engine
                                                                             │
                                                                       Calculate Scores
                                                                             │
                                                                   Return Trade Proposals
```

---

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `filatelia-web/db/migrations/0006_user_collections.sql` | Create | D1 SQL migration script defining `UserCollection` table, CHECK constraints, and performance indexes. |
| `filatelia-web/src/types/collection.ts` | Create | TypeScript type definitions for collection items, condition grades, list types, and API payloads. |
| `filatelia-web/src/lib/auth-google.ts` | Create | Google OAuth PKCE token exchange helper functions and user profile mapping. |
| `filatelia-web/src/app/api/auth/google/route.ts` | Create | Edge Route Handler managing Google OAuth 2.0 redirection and callback authentication. |
| `filatelia-web/src/app/api/collection/route.ts` | Create | Edge Route Handler for `/api/collection` endpoints (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). |
| `filatelia-web/src/app/api/match/route.ts` | Create | Edge Route Handler for `/api/match` computing 2-way reciprocal collection matches. |
| `filatelia-web/src/app/perfil/PerfilClient.tsx` | Modify | Upgrade user profile with 3-tab inventory UI (`Colección`, `Deseos`, `Intercambio`), condition badges, and trade match list. |
| `filatelia-web/src/app/(public)/catalogo/CatalogoClient.tsx` | Modify | Add quick-toggle collection action buttons to catalog stamp cards. |

---

## Interfaces / Contracts

### D1 Migration Schema v6 (`0006_user_collections.sql`)

```sql
-- Migration 0006: Create UserCollection table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS UserCollection (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  stamp_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  list_type TEXT CHECK(list_type IN ('collection', 'wishlist', 'trade')) NOT NULL,
  condition TEXT CHECK(condition IN ('MNH', 'MH', 'Used', 'FDC')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MNH',
  notes TEXT,
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  UNIQUE(user_id, stamp_id, list_type)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_collection_user_type ON UserCollection(user_id, list_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_collection_stamp ON UserCollection(stamp_id);
```

### TypeScript Definitions (`src/types/collection.ts`)

```typescript
export type ListType = 'collection' | 'wishlist' | 'trade';
export type ConditionGrade = 'MNH' | 'MH' | 'Used' | 'FDC';

export interface UserCollectionItem {
  id: number;
  userId: string;
  stampId: string;
  listType: ListType;
  condition: ConditionGrade;
  notes?: string;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  stampTitle?: string;
  stampImage?: string;
  stampCatalogNumber?: string;
}

export interface CollectionRequestPayload {
  stampId: string;
  listType: ListType;
  condition?: ConditionGrade;
  notes?: string;
}

export interface MatchProposal {
  partnerUserId: string;
  partnerName: string;
  partnerEmail: string;
  matchScore: number;
  itemsYouGet: string[];
  itemsYouGive: string[];
}
```

---

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Unit | `auth-google.ts` PKCE state & token validation | Verify state parameter verification and token payload extraction logic. |
| Unit | Trade Match Algorithm (`/api/match`) | Test set intersection, reciprocal check (`|M_AB| > 0 AND |M_BA| > 0`), and percentage calculation against mock datasets. |
| Integration | `/api/collection` CRUD routes | Execute POST, GET, PUT, DELETE against local D1 SQLite testing environment with simulated `fp_session` cookies. |
| Integration | Schema Constraints (D1 v6) | Verify rejection of invalid `list_type` or `condition` values and enforcement of unique `(user_id, stamp_id, list_type)` constraint. |
| E2E | `/perfil` 3-Tab UI & Quick Catalog Actions | Playwright test suite validating tab switching, condition updating, and catalog quick-add toggle buttons. |

---

## Threat Matrix

| Boundary Category | Status | Expected Safe / Failure Behavior | Planned RED Tests |
|-------------------|--------|----------------------------------|-------------------|
| Routing & OAuth Redirects | **Applicable** | Rejects invalid OAuth `state` parameter or unverified redirect URIs with HTTP 400. CSRF state token enforced. | `test_oauth_invalid_state_rejected`: Attempt OAuth callback with forged state token; assert 400 response and zero session creation. |
| Session & Auth Middleware | **Applicable** | Protected routes (`/api/collection`, `/api/match`) return HTTP 401 Unauthorized when `fp_session` cookie is missing or invalid. | `test_collection_api_unauthenticated_rejected`: Issue GET/POST to `/api/collection` with no headers; assert HTTP 401. |
| Input Validation & Injection | **Applicable** | Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection. Invalid `list_type` or `condition` rejected by API validation and D1 SQL CHECK constraints. | `test_collection_invalid_enum_rejected`: Submit POST payload with `list_type = 'stolen'`; assert HTTP 400 validation error. |
| Executable / Subprocess Execution | **N/A** | N/A — No subprocess execution, system binaries, or external executable shell invocation in collection-and-automatch. | N/A — No executable boundaries present. |
| VCS / PR Automation | **N/A** | N/A — System does not execute VCS commands or GitHub PR actions automatically. | N/A — No VCS boundaries present. |

---

## Migration / Rollout

1. **Database Migration**: Run Cloudflare D1 migration v6 via Wrangler:  
   `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply filatelia-db --local` (and `--remote` in production).
2. **Environment Variables**: Configure `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in environment secret store.
3. **Deployment**: Deploy edge functions and Next.js frontend to Cloudflare Pages.
4. **Verification**: Verify session generation, collection list additions on `/perfil`, and reciprocal trade proposals on `/api/match`.

---

## Open Questions

- [x] Should condition default to 'MNH' if unspecified? (Yes, 'MNH' is the standard default for unused stamps).
- [x] Are trades restricted to reciprocal matches only? (Yes, reciprocal match requires |M_AB| > 0 AND |M_BA| > 0).

y esto tambien afecta 2. CONFIGURACIÓN DE CORS EN EL BACKEND
En backend/src/main.ts, el backend filtra los orígenes permitidos mediante la variable FRONTEND_URL. Si en la VM (/opt/traceexport/produccion-infra/.env) esa variable sigue apuntando a http://localhost:3001 o a la IP vieja, NestJS rechazará cualquier petición proveniente de https://app.escorpia.com.

Solución: En el .env de la VM, actualizá: FRONTEND_URL=https://app.escorpia.com.
3. ATRIBUTOS DE LAS COOKIES (SameSite y Secure)
La autenticación de tu sistema utiliza cookies de sesión HTTP-only (access_token y refresh_token). En auth.service.ts, las cookies se configuran con COOKIE_SECURE, COOKIE_SAMESITE y COOKIE_DOMAIN.

Solución: Al estar en dominios con HTTPS, en el .env de la VM debés configurar:
env
COOKIE_SECURE=true
COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax
COOKIE_DOMAIN=.escorpia.com
(El punto al inicio de .escorpia.com permite compartir cookies entre app.escorpia.com y api.escorpia.com).

ya hice lo que me dices en otra evalucion tambien me dijeron esto EL PROBLEMA TÉCNICO: REESCRITURA DE SUBDOMINIO (MULTITENANCY)
En src/proxy.ts, tenés esta lógica para manejar subdominios por cliente (tenant):

typescript
const rootDomain = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_ROOT_DOMAIN ?? 'localhost'
const tenantSlug = hostname !== rootDomain && hostname.endsWith(`.${rootDomain}`)
  ? hostname.replace(`.${rootDomain}`, '')
  : null
¿Qué está pasando en producción?

Al entrar a https://app.escorpia.com, el middleware detecta que el dominio termina en .escorpia.com.
Como el sistema cree que cualquier subdominio es un cliente (tenant), asume que "app" es el nombre de la empresa (tenant) en lugar del subdominio principal de la aplicación.
Al entrar a https://app.escorpia.com/login, el middleware reescribe la ruta internamente a https://app.escorpia.com/app/login. Como la ruta /app/login no existe en las carpetas de Next.js, te tira un 404 This page could not be found.
Al entrar a https://app.escorpia.com/, reescribe a https://app.escorpia.com/app, abriéndote el panel dinámico [tenant] tratando a "app" como la empresa.
CÓMO SOLUCIONARLO (2 OPCIONES)
Opción A (Sin tocar código — En Vercel): En las variables de entorno de Vercel, configurá:

env
NEXT_PUBLIC_ROOT_DOMAIN=app.escorpia.com
Al hacer esto, hostname y rootDomain serán iguales (app.escorpia.com), por lo que el middleware no tratará a app como un cliente y la navegación https://app.escorpia.com/login y /perufrost funcionará impecable.

Opción B (En el código — src/proxy.ts): Excluir explícitamente app y www para que el middleware nunca los interprete como slugs de empresa:

typescript
const tenantSlug = hostname !== rootDomain && 
  hostname.endsWith(`.${rootDomain}`) && 
  !hostname.startsWith('app.') && 
  !hostname.startsWith('www.')
    ? hostname.replace(`.${rootDomain}`, '')
    : null

## Findings

**WARNING (real) — Inline edit of `orden_compra`/`shrinkage_pct` silently reverts payment status and asset state**
File: `backend/src/modules/acopio/services/acopio-general-view-edit.service.ts` (price branch) + `backend/src/modules/acopio/services/acopio-weighing.service.ts:149` (`setPrice`)
Description: Any price-group edit (`real_price`, `shrinkage_pct`, `orden_compra`) routes through `weighing.setPrice()`, which unconditionally executes `payment_status = 'PENDIENTE'` and transitions `status PESADO→CON_PRECIO`. So an admin correcting the `orden_compra` on a row already marked `PAGADO` silently reverts it to `PENDIENTE`. The general view exposes `orden_compra` as an independent editable cell, making this a normal, easily-triggered path — a real data-integrity regression on already-paid receptions.
Suggested fix: In the edit service, when only `orden_compra`/`shrinkage_pct` change (no real price change), use a narrower update that preserves `payment_status`, or add a dedicated `setPurchaseOrder` that does not reset payment.

**WARNING (real) — `payment_status` inline edit has no value validation → raw 500 on invalid input**
File: `backend/src/modules/acopio/services/acopio-general-view-edit.service.ts` (`paymentStatus = edit.value as ...`) + `acopio-weighing.service.ts:183` (`markPaymentStatus`)
Description: The column is `editable` with type `text`, rendered as a free-text `<Input>` in the frontend. The edit service casts `edit.value` to the union without checking; `markPaymentStatus` writes it raw. The DB column has `CHECK (payment_status IN ('POR_GENERAR','PENDIENTE','PAGADO'))` (migration `001_create.sql:179`). Typing anything else (the natural thing for a plain text cell) produces a Postgres CHECK violation surfaced as an unhandled 500, not a domain `400`. It also allows setting `'POR_GENERAR'`, which this path never intends.
Suggested fix: Validate `value ∈ {'PENDIENTE','PAGADO'}` in `resolveGeneralViewEditColumn`/edit service and throw `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; render a select on the frontend for that column.

**WARNING (real) — Numeric columns sort lexicographically (wrong order) because `wide` projects them as `::text`**
File: `backend/src/modules/acopio/services/acopio-arrivals.service.ts:1677-1682` etc. + `helpers/general-view-query.helper.ts` (`resolveGeneralViewSortColumn`) + service `ORDER BY "${sortColumn}"`
Description: Every numeric column (`gross_weight`, `net_weight`, `real_price`, `estimated_quantity`, `total_importe`, `shrinkage_pct`, …) is projected as text in the `wide` CTE. `sortBy` is whitelisted for ALL columns and `ORDER BY "net_weight" DESC` therefore sorts strings: `'9' > '100' > '1000'`. The design explicitly lists `sortBy` as a supported API capability, so any consumer sorting a numeric column receives incorrect ordering. (The shipped frontend does not yet wire a sort control, so it is not user-triggerable through the current UI, but the endpoint contract is wrong.)
Suggested fix: Order by the underlying typed expression, not the text alias — e.g. keep a typed `sortExpr` per registry column, or cast back (`ORDER BY (\"net_weight\")::numeric`) for numeric/date types.

**WARNING (real) — Doc-field inline edits bleed into sibling flat-metadata columns (`eslora`, `armador_nombre`)**
File: `backend/src/modules/acopio/services/acopio-documents.service.ts:781-800` (`saveValidation` flattening, committed version) surfaced by `general-view-columns.ts` + wide SQL
Description: `saveValidation` writes BOTH the namespaced composite key AND a flattened bare key into `aa.metadata` (`merged = {...flatExtractedFields, ...dto.extractedFields, ...}`). The general view shows these as distinct columns that read the flat key: `eslora` reads `aa.metadata->>'eslora'`, `armador_nombre` reads `aa.metadata->>'representante_armador'`. Editing the doc columns `eslora_permiso` (`PERMISO_PESCA:eslora`) or `representante_armador` (`PERMISO_PESCA:representante_armador`) also overwrites the flat keys, so the separate `eslora`/`armador_nombre` cells change to the permit value. The collision is pre-existing in `saveValidation`, but this feature is the first surface that displays both columns side-by-side, making the corruption visible and reachable.
Suggested fix: Stop writing flat keys for namespaced doc fields, or have the metadata-extra columns read a disambiguated key; at minimum document/flag the overlap for these two columns.

## Resumen

Se agregó al gate **DOC_OK** un nuevo check (paso 5) que exige que los documentos de biblioteca (permiso/SANIPES) de cada entidad del alcance tengan el **PDF subido** (`storage_path IS NOT NULL`), antes del avance a `DOC_OK`.

### Archivos modificados
- `/home/rodrigo/Documentos/trabajos/Escorpiatraza/backend/src/core/errors/error-codes.ts` — nuevo código `LIBRARY_DOCS_NOT_UPLOADED`.
